stories.title: Scientists create 'super ice' that is ten times stronger and far harder to shatter
stories.summary: Scientists have developed a reinforced ice material called BioPykrete that is about ten times stronger than ordinary ice. Phys Org reports that the material can absorb roughly seventy times more energy before breaking. The research was led by Professor Ido Braslavsky of the Hebrew University Robert H. Smith Faculty of Agriculture, Food and Environment. The team created the new material by mixing ice with cellulose nanocrystals and adding an engineered chimeric protein. This protein acts as molecular glue to bind the ice and cellulose together at the molecular level. Laboratory tests showed that adding this engineered protein doubled both the strength and energy absorption compared to a similar mixture without the molecular bridge. Braslavsky stated that they wanted to go beyond simply mixing fibers into ice and instead control how the different materials connect at the molecular level. He noted that the result changes not only how strong the ice is, but also how it breaks by absorbing much more energy and deforming gradually. The biodegradable material offers a lower-carbon construction alternative for extremely cold regions where transporting traditional building supplies remains expensive.
stories.stakes: The biodegradable material offers a lower-carbon construction alternative for extremely cold regions where transporting traditional building supplies remains expensive.

stories.title: India deeply concerned about blockades in Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb, says govt.
stories.summary:
India is deeply concerned by blockades in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and the Strait of Hormuz, the Ministry of External Affairs said on Tuesday, September fifteenth, twenty twenty-six, according to The Hindu. More than two point four million Indians live and work in Saudi Arabia while several regional cities remain on alert due to ongoing attacks. A ship carrying fourteen Indian seafarers was targeted off the Oman coast on Sunday. Omani authorities are assisting with search operations for a missing Indian seafarer after the vessel carrying twenty-three crew members was hit. Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated we deeply thank the Omani authorities for rescuing our nationals and our embassy in Muscat is in close touch. Blockades threaten the safety of millions of citizens abroad, regional stability, freedom of navigation, and vital international commerce waterways.

The developments were discussed when External Affairs Minister S. Jai-shun-kur and Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud met during the B. R. I. C. S. Summit in Delhi. Prime Minister Nuh-ren-druh Moe-dee also met with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the summit to discuss mutual concerns and regional stability.
stories.stakes: Blockades threaten the safety of millions of citizens abroad, regional stability, freedom of navigation, and vital international commerce waterways.

stories.title: Advanced X-ray crystallography determines structure of macromolecule at unprecedented resolution
stories.summary: Scientists led by Ashwin Chari from the Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences in Gottingen, Germany, have successfully determined the structure of the archaeal rubredoxin protein. Phys Org reports that the team reached a resolution of zero point four three angstroms. International researchers from several institutions contributed to the milestone. The researchers utilized P. E. T. R. A. three at D. E. S. Y. in Hamburg, alongside advanced software and low dose protocols. This technological combination allowed the team to map accurate nuclear positions and observe quantum mechanical phenomena directly from the experimental structure. This breakthrough represents the highest resolution protein structure yet determined, bridging structural biology and quantum chemistry for future research.
stories.stakes: This breakthrough represents the highest resolution protein structure yet determined, bridging structural biology and quantum chemistry for future research.

stories.title: Drug Control raids expose painkiller sale violations at 55 medical shops in Andhra Pradesh
stories.summary: State authorities inspected one hundred medical shops across Andhra Pradesh following an arrest in Eluru district last week. The Drug Control Administration launched these checks after five people allegedly sold the pain reliever Tramadol without prescriptions, The Hindu reports. Violations turned up at fifty-five shops, including two major cases involving large quantities of medicines handled without relevant bills. Officials seized seven thousand five hundred fifty Tramadol injections from Lakshmi Srinivasa Medical Agency due to missing sale records. Another firm, D. Roopa Peddinti Medical Agency, bought five thousand two hundred Tramec injections over two years using fraudulent billing. Director-General Arun Babu stated that licences of those involved would be cancelled alongside strict legal action. The crackdown threatens pharmacy operating licenses and signals aggressive enforcement against unauthorized sales of controlled painkillers across the state.
stories.stakes: The crackdown threatens pharmacy operating licenses and signals aggressive enforcement against unauthorized sales of controlled painkillers across the state.

stories.title: Trump administration orders Kalshi to scrap AI price tracker over national security concerns
stories.summary: The United States Commerce Department ordered Kalshi to take down its A. I. compute future curve product last month over national security concerns. Semafor reports that commerce officials directed the company to unpublish the tracker, which pulls together data on the cost to rent Nvidia chips. Separately, commerce officials pushed the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to freeze approval of new compute contracts for sixty days. The regulatory intervention freezes nascent compute contracts, disrupting billions in borrowing by neoclouds using older chip prices as collateral. Startup executives maintain that compute is going to be the next big commodity in the world as demand for infrastructure and processing power continues to shape the broader financial landscape.
stories.author: Reed Albergotti
stories.stakes: The regulatory intervention freezes nascent compute contracts, disrupting billions in borrowing by neoclouds using older chip prices as collateral.

stories.title: Champions League final venues revealed: Munich 2028, Barcelona 2029
stories.summary: The Allianz Arena in Munich and Camp Nou in Barcelona will host the Champions League finals in twenty twenty-eight and twenty twenty-nine. European football governing body U. E. F. A. announced the venues on Tuesday, according to Aljazeera. The Allianz Arena will stage its third Champions League final in twenty twenty-eight. Redevelopment work continues at Camp Nou as part of a revamp project launched in twenty twenty-three. Bayern Munich chief executive officer Jan-Christian Dreesen stated that this is fantastic news for the club. Barcelona president Joan Laporta stated that it is an immense pride for the team and all fans. Women's Champions League finals will take place at Parc Olympique Lyonnais in twenty twenty-eight and Cardiff's Principality Stadium in twenty twenty-nine. Madrid's Estadio Metropolitano is scheduled to host the twenty twenty-six to twenty twenty-seven campaign final on June fifth. The stadium selections secure high-profile tourism and broadcast revenues for Munich, Barcelona, Lee-on, and Cardiff through the end of the decade.
stories.stakes: The stadium selections secure high-profile tourism and broadcast revenues for Munich, Barcelona, Lyon, and Cardiff through the end of the decade.

stories.title: Rapid data center expansion incites backlash in Republican stronghold
stories.summary: With just a couple months to go until the U. S. midterm election, a new political fault line is emerging in Republican strongholds across Texas. This rising tension is driven by the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure in the state, France 24 Top reports. Nearly sixty percent of planned new data centers are set to be built directly within congressional districts that voted for Donald Trump in twenty twenty-four. Driven by the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence, the A. I. boom is now sparking a backlash from some of the voters who helped put him back in office. The infrastructure boom in Republican strongholds complicates political loyalties for conservative lawmakers facing grassroots backlash over resource demands.
stories.author: Pierrick LEURENT
stories.stakes: The infrastructure boom in Republican strongholds complicates political loyalties for conservative lawmakers facing grassroots backlash over resource demands.

stories.title: Musk urges top AI labs, Chinese companies to test each other's models amid calls for slowdown
stories.summary: Elon Musk spoke at the All-In Summit in Los Angeles on Monday. He urged x. A. I., Open A. I., An-throw-pick, Google, Meta, and leading Chinese companies to test each other's models before public release. Instead of grading your own homework, you would have competitors grading your homework, Musk stated, according to Cnbc Top. SpaceX acquired x. A. I. in February. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump called fears over artificial intelligence a hoax and a scam in social media posts on Monday. National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett stated that the private sector is the right place to address concerns with artificial intelligence. The government continues to monitor the industry and will use law enforcement when necessary to make sure firms act responsibly. Cross-company model testing by competitors could reshape industry accountability, while the administration signals a preference for private sector self-regulation.
stories.stakes: Cross-company model testing by competitors could reshape industry accountability, while the administration signals a preference for private sector self-regulation.

stories.title: Trump’s 4-year US student visa rule blocked: What it means for Indian students
stories.summary:
A United States federal judge temporarily blocked a Trump administration rule replacing the duration of status system for foreign students. Massachusetts District Judge F. Dennis Saylor the fourth issued the ruling just a day before the Department of Homeland Security rule was scheduled to take effect, Livemint reports. The judge wrote that the damage to the higher education system and to the economy of the United States is likely to be catastrophic. The Open Doors twenty twenty-five report cited in the case material showed that three hundred sixty-three thousand and nineteen Indian students were enrolled during the twenty twenty-four to twenty twenty-five academic year. Indian students account for nearly thirty-one percent of all international students in the country. The blocked rule would have generally limited F-one and J-one admissions to the length of the programme subject to a maximum of four years. Harvard President Alan Garber questioned the four-year limit by noting that a typical P. H. D. can take at least six years. The preliminary injunction protects hundreds of thousands of Indian students from sudden immigration changes while their legal challenges continue through the courts.

The ruling provides temporary relief to international students while the underlying legal challenge continues through the courts. Students who are already in the country can continue to operate under the existing framework for now. The decision temporarily prevents the new system from taking effect across more than five thousand higher education institutions operating across the United States. The ruling is a preliminary injunction, meaning the underlying legal battle is still underway and rules could change depending on the final outcome.
stories.stakes: The preliminary injunction protects hundreds of thousands of Indian students from sudden immigration changes while their legal challenges continue through the courts.

stories.title: Roman roads weren’t so straight after all
stories.summary: A digital reconstruction of the ancient Roman road network challenges centuries-old assumptions that all roads lead to Rome and are uniformly straight. Tom Brughmans at Aarhus University notes that these are widely held assumptions, even among academics, according to New Scientist. Last year, researchers used topographic mapping, satellite imagery, and historical sources to create a map of roads in the Roman Empire in A. D. one hundred and fifty, totalling almost three hundred thousand kilometres in length. The analysis reveals that Roman roads were mostly straight only where the landscape permitted, such as lowland regions in western Europe and North Africa. Major modern roads tend to be straighter than ancient roads because they facilitate faster travel by car. Around ninety percent of Roman roads were built with a slope gradient that could permit the passage of animal-driven carts and wagons, including through the Alps. Brughmans states that this suggests the Romans were dedicated to maintaining and improving overland accessibility and connectivity on an empire-wide scale. Meanwhile, Rome wasn't as central as the medieval proverb suggests, with provincial capitals consistently serving as key crossroads mediating overland communications in their respective provinces. Ray Laurence at Macquarie University states that the correlation between the ancient and modern networks shows that the Romans created the future geography of Europe. The digital reconstruction challenges academic assumptions about ancient infrastructure by proving provincial capitals served as key crossroads rather than Rome.
stories.author: James Urquhart
stories.stakes: The digital reconstruction challenges academic assumptions about ancient infrastructure by proving provincial capitals served as key crossroads rather than Rome.

stories.title: How better ways of screening drugs could soon lead to thousands fewer animal tests
stories.summary:
As many as one hundred ninety million animals are used in biomedical research around the world every year. Modern biomedical research has relied on animals almost since its inception to study disease and test new medicines before they ever reach people. However, efforts to replace animals in science now have firm backing from policy-makers and regulators, New Scientist reports.

In April twenty twenty-five, the U. S. Food and Drug Administration published a five-year road map to reduce animal testing in drug safety studies. Months later, the countrys National Institutes of Health stopped requiring animal models for many of its grants. Late last year, the United Kingdom launched a similar plan to phase out animal testing, and the European Union followed suit in June. Global regulatory shifts and new organ chip technologies will phase out animal testing across pharmaceutical research sectors.

Public opinion has shifted alongside these policy changes. In two thousand one, most Americans believed medical testing on animals was morally acceptable, but by twenty twenty-five fewer than half did. Regulatory agencies and scientists are now turning toward alternative methods, such as organs-on-a-chip, cell cultures, and artificial intelligence models, to screen drugs and identify potential targets without using animals. More than ninety per cent of experimental drugs that appear safe and effective in animals do not receive regulatory approval, largely because they turn out to be toxic to humans.

In twenty twenty-two, biologist Donald Ingber at Harvard University and his colleagues built and tested a liver-on-a-chip that identified nearly seven out of every eight drugs that proved toxic in clinical trials despite appearing safe in animal tests. The pharmaceutical company Moderna has used it in place of primates to screen compounds used in messenger R. N. A. vaccines for liver damage. The science has reached a point where there is a much better evidence base to support the fact that phasing out much animal testing might be possible, says Celean Camp, head of the United Kingdom campaign group Replacing Animal Research. The new road maps and technological advancements aim to build on this progress to develop more non-animal regulatory tests and meaningfully reduce animal testing.
stories.author: David Adam
stories.stakes: Global regulatory shifts and new organ chip technologies will phase out animal testing across pharmaceutical research sectors.

stories.title: Clarity Act could overhaul US crypto, stablecoin rules: What the bill changes and why it matters | Explained
stories.summary: The United States Senate is scheduled to vote on Tuesday on whether to advance the Clarity Act. Livemint reports that the legislative vote tests whether Republican leaders can secure the sixty votes needed to move the bill forward. Senate Republicans released a revised version of the bill on Sunday to address concerns from banks and Democrats. President Donald Trump disclosed in June that he had made one point four billion dollars from his crypto ventures. Banks oppose stablecoin provisions because allowing stablecoins to compete with traditional bank deposits could harm bank lending. Crypto companies strongly back the legislation because clearer regulations would reduce legal uncertainty and provide a firmer foundation for digital asset businesses. The Senate vote on the Clarity Act tests whether lawmakers can secure sixty votes to establish a new regulatory framework for cryptocurrency.
stories.stakes: The Senate vote on the Clarity Act tests whether lawmakers can secure sixty votes to establish a new regulatory framework for cryptocurrency.

stories.title: Spanish scientists find first evidence of Diplodocus dinosaur in Europe
stories.summary: Researchers from the Dinopolis Foundation found the first skeletal evidence of the Diplodocus dinosaur outside North America. The fossils include fourteen caudal vertebrae and several chevron bones dating back around one hundred and fifty million years. They were uncovered at the La Tejeria site in eastern Spain, according to Dw Top. A new study published this week concludes the find is one of the most complete diplodocid skeletons from Europe. Systematic analysis reveals the remains can be confidently referred to as Diplodocus. This discovery serves as strong evidence supporting episodic dispersal events and faunal exchanges across the proto-North Atlantic Ocean. This proves prehistoric animals crossed temporary land connections between separating continents during the late Kimmeridgian and early Tithonian periods.
stories.stakes: This discovery proves temporary land connections existed across the proto-North Atlantic Ocean, reshaping our understanding of prehistoric global dinosaur migration.

stories.title: India ends free ride for larger transactions on its ubiquitous digital payments network
stories.summary: India will impose a zero point four percent merchant fee on certain Unified Payments Interface payments above two thousand rupees starting October fifteenth. The National Payments Corporation of India stated that consumers will continue to use the digital payments service for free. Techcrunch reports that the new merchant fee is capped at three hundred rupees for transactions of seventy-five thousand rupees or more. Small merchants receiving up to one hundred thousand rupees a month through the network will be exempt from the charges. The move aims to make the digital payments system financially self-sustaining by covering the growing cost of operating the network. Industry estimates put the annual cost of running the network at about two hundred billion rupees. The network processed twenty-four point five one billion transactions worth twenty-nine point nine trillion rupees in August alone. The newly announced merchant fees will be distributed among participants in the payments ecosystem and used to fund investments in infrastructure, cybersecurity, fraud prevention, and customer service. Krishnamurthy Subramanian questioned the policy on X by asking what the opportunity cost and social benefits of charging transactions are. Subramanian noted that the network should be treated as digital public infrastructure whose benefits extend well beyond individual transactions, including by reducing reliance on cash, bringing more businesses into the formal economy, and widening access to digital payments. Payments of up to two thousand rupees account for more than ninety-five percent of merchant transactions by volume on the network. Merchants will not be allowed to pass the fee on to customers, according to the network operator, which argued that the charge is low enough for businesses to absorb while consumers continue to pay the listed price regardless of whether they use the service. The zero point four percent merchant fee alters digital payment economics for Indian businesses processing over two thousand rupees monthly.
stories.author: Jagmeet Singh
stories.stakes: The zero point four percent merchant fee alters digital payment economics for Indian businesses processing over two thousand rupees monthly.

stories.title: Fee on UPI payments above Rs 2,000: Who pays and what changes for you
stories.summary: A merchant discount rate of zero point four percent will apply on person-to-merchant U. P. I. transactions above two thousand rupees starting October fifteenth, twenty twenty-six. According to the Times Of India, this change is detailed in a notification from N. P. C. I. For transactions of seventy-five thousand rupees and above, the rate will be capped at three hundred rupees per transaction. Person-to-person transactions will continue to be completely free of cost for both payers and beneficiaries. Small-value U. P. I. transactions up to two thousand rupees comprise more than ninety-five percent of the total volume of U. P. I. person-to-merchant transactions. Ordinary consumers will not be charged for making payments via U. P. I., and U. P. I. applications are explicitly restricted from levying platform fees on U. P. I. transactions. N. P. C. I. stated that the intent of levying reasonable merchant discount rates is to ensure that U. P. I. remains accessible and convenient for everyday transactions. The new merchant discount rate shifts transaction costs to businesses while protecting ordinary consumers from fees on everyday payments. The merchant discount rate is being introduced to invest in infrastructure resiliency, innovation, cybersecurity, and customer service.
stories.author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
stories.stakes: The new merchant discount rate shifts transaction costs to businesses while protecting ordinary consumers from fees on everyday payments.

stories.title: 10-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2007 as traders bet a Fed rate hike is coming
stories.summary:
The bench marks ten-year Treasury yield climbed to five point zero four one percent on Tuesday, reaching its highest level since July two thousand and seven. The thirty-year Treasury bond yield rose to a high of five point four zero one percent, also hitting its highest level since June two thousand and seven.

Traders are pricing in a more than ninety-two percent chance that the Federal Reserve will raise rates by twenty-five basis points, Cnbc Top reports. U. S. ten-year treasuries are highly sensitive to inflation expectations. Jonathan Liang, Standard Chartered chief investment officer of fixed income and foreign exchange, stated that with inflation gauges still above the Federal Reserve target of two percent, this tight correlation will likely persist for a while. Higher Treasury yields increase borrowing costs for corporate funding and consumer loans across the broader economy.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil topped one hundred and two dollars a barrel on Tuesday as the Iran conflict drags on and the Strait of Hormuz remains essentially blocked. Meanwhile, National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett told C. N. B. C. on Tuesday that he believes inflation is showing signs of cooling based on near-term memory and the stochastic process that drives inflation.
stories.stakes: Higher Treasury yields increase borrowing costs for corporate funding and consumer loans across the broader economy.

stories.title: Alappad panchayat in Keralam’s Kollam prepares for UNESCO Tsunami Ready status
stories.summary: A comprehensive mock drill was conducted on Tuesday across wards fourteen, fifteen, and sixteen. The exercise is part of preparations to secure tsunami ready recognition for Alappad grama panchayat in Kollam, according to The Hindu. The initiative is jointly implemented by the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, along with national and state disaster management authorities. The exercise commenced at nine thirty a.m. when a tsunami alert was issued from the state authority to the district authority. Led by panchayat president, S. Jayasree, officials evacuated residents from the beach vicinity to a safe designated area near the Mukkumpuzha Devi temple. Vulnerable individuals received special attention from fire and rescue personnel and Aapda Mitra volunteers before evacuees were shifted to a relief camp at the Doctor V. V. Velukutty Arayan Government Regional Fisheries Technical High School supported by a medical team. The coastal security drill prepares local residents across three wards for tsunami emergencies ahead of international certification.
stories.stakes: The coastal security drill prepares local residents across three wards for tsunami emergencies ahead of international certification.

stories.title: EPA seeks to eliminate remaining greenhouse-gas rules for power plants
stories.summary:
The Trump administration overturned most of a Biden-era rule limiting climate pollution from power plants. Ars Science reports that the Environmental Protection Agency announced a final plan to gut the twenty twenty-four Carbon Pollution Standards. The agency stated that the previous regulations exceed its authority under the Clean Air Act. The reversal lowers compliance costs for power plant operators by eliminating mandatory carbon pollution standards established under the previous administration.

The agency claims the previous rules require control technologies that are not adequately demonstrated and deliver three hundred billion dollars in savings. The agency also proposed revoking all remaining greenhouse gas emissions requirements for power plants. Officials argued that these emissions have no material impact on climate change. The plan to revoke the standards was initially revealed last spring following warnings about rising global temperatures from a United Nations report and the hottest summer on record.
stories.author: Liza Gross, Inside Climate News
stories.stakes: The reversal lowers compliance costs for power plant operators by eliminating mandatory carbon pollution standards established under the previous administration.

stories.title: China, Russia warn against ‘weaponisation’ of space after US confirms orbital weapons
stories.summary: China and Russia warned against the militarisation of outer space on Tuesday after the United States confirmed it has weapons in orbit. Livemint reports that China urged the United States to stop expanding its military capabilities. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called for international work toward complete demilitarisation. The warnings followed an acknowledgment by the United States Space Force that Washington possesses on-orbit space control weapons to defend forces. These capabilities include kinetic and non-kinetic means to affect adversary space systems. The American acknowledgment of orbital weapons risks accelerating an arms race and military competition in space with China and Russia.
stories.stakes: The American acknowledgment of orbital weapons risks accelerating an arms race and military competition in space with China and Russia.

stories.title: Merchants to now pay fees on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 from Oct 15
stories.summary: The National Payments Corporation of India notified a merchant discount rate of zero point four percent on person-to-merchant U. P. I. transactions above two thousand rupees. The new rate becomes effective on October fifteenth, twenty twenty-six, according to Times Of India, giving acquiring banks and payment aggregators adequate time to update their software. Transactions of seventy-five thousand rupees and above will face a cap of three hundred rupees. Small-value payments up to two thousand rupees remain unaffected, while person-to-person transfers stay completely free. The new merchant discount rate provides predictable revenue for payment aggregators and banks while protecting small-value consumer transactions from fees. Finance Minister Nirmala Sith-a-ra-mun assured parliament that consumers will not pay fees for everyday payments, following amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act of two thousand seven.
stories.author: TOI BUSINESS DESK
stories.stakes: The new merchant discount rate provides predictable revenue for payment aggregators and banks while protecting small-value consumer transactions from fees.

stories.title: Robinhood To Offer Share Redemptions And Voting Rights On Tokenized Stocks
stories.summary: Online brokerage Robinhood Markets plans to offer share redemptions and voting rights on tokenized stocks. Chief Executive Officer Vlad Tenev announced the move in a social media post on September fourteenth. Yahoo Finance reports that the company is actively working on redemptions for shares one-to-one with voting for eligible token holders. Movie theatre chain A.M. C. Entertainment criticized Robinhood and called on the brokerage to stop offering a tokenized stock version. A.M.C. stated it has not approved the tokenized stock version and that token holders lack the rights of other shareholders. Providing in-kind redemptions allows investors to exchange a tokenized stock for a corresponding share. Voting rights help ease investor concerns and grant holders of tokenized stocks the same rights as other shareholders. Robinhood stock trades at one hundred fourteen dollars and thirty-three cents US per share and is down zero point four four percent over the last twelve months. Robinhood offering redemptions and voting rights on tokenized stocks addresses criticism from movie theatre chain A.M.C. Entertainment.
stories.stakes: Robinhood offering redemptions and voting rights on tokenized stocks addresses criticism from movie theatre chain A.M.C. Entertainment.

stories.title: Two sailors missing after tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz, Oman says
stories.summary:
Two sailors are missing and twenty-three others were rescued following an attack on an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. Oman states, according to Bbc World, that the Panama flagged El Gaia was towed to an Omani port on Tuesday after a fire broke out in its engine room. Iran claimed the tanker hit naval mines. The United States military stated it was struck by an Iranian missile last month and a drone over the weekend. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupts global oil transport and escalates shipping risks across the strategic maritime corridor.

The International Maritime Organization reported that at least twenty-two seafarers have been killed in seventy-nine confirmed incidents in the region since February. The Strait of Hormuz has effectively closed due to Iranian attacks on commercial vessels and a United States naval blockade. Meanwhile, Iranian small boats recently attempted to take possession of a United States unmanned surface vessel, but they were unsuccessful after Centcom forcefully responded.
stories.stakes: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupts global oil transport and escalates shipping risks across the strategic maritime corridor.

stories.title: London loses bid to host 2029 World Athletics as Nairobi named host
stories.summary: London has missed out to Nairobi in the bid to host the twenty twenty-nine World Athletics Championships. Bbc Sport reports that an African city will host the event for the first time in history. The decision was confirmed at a World Athletics council meeting in Budapest where Munich was also confirmed as the host for the twenty thirty-one event. World Athletics president Sebastian Coe stated that Nairobi had presented a compelling and emotional bid. London missed out on the twenty twenty-nine hosting rights despite securing forty-five million pounds in public money and proposing the London Stadium as the host venue through a bid led by Athletic Ventures. Jack Buckner stated that U. K. Athletics was deeply disappointed that the championships will not be held in London and that they believed they had an outstanding bid which would genuinely take the sport to new levels. Amber Anning expressed disappointment that London missed out on hosting the event as a home competition while noting that having the championships in Africa for the first time will be really special. Taking the event to Africa fulfills the mission of growing athletics worldwide across Asia, Africa, and Europe over the next three editions while marking a historic milestone for the continent.
stories.stakes: Hosting the event in Africa for the first time marks a historic milestone that fulfills the global growth mission across multiple continents.

stories.title: US admits to having weapons in orbit: How do they work, and should Russia, China worry?
stories.summary: The United States has acknowledged for the first time that it has weapons deployed in orbit, revealing a previously undisclosed military capability in space. United States Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink stated on Monday, according to Livemint, that Washington possesses on-orbit space control weapons to protect American forces from hostile action. Meink made the disclosure during the Air and Space Forces Association conference held in Maryland. The decision to reveal the existence of the weapon was deliberate and intended to deter potential adversaries. He declined to discuss specific design details, capabilities, testing, or potential targets at a subsequent press roundtable. The United States Space Force later stated that space control missions involve both kinetic and non-kinetic methods aimed at challenging and controlling activity in orbit. Such capabilities could be used to disrupt, degrade, or destroy an adversary space system, serving both offensive and defensive purposes. Victoria Samson of the Secure World Foundation told the Financial Times that the weapon could be a space-based jammer. Clayton Swope of the Center for Strategic and International Studies noted that countries such as China and Russia are considered potential threats to American interests in space. In twenty twenty-five, President Donald Trump signed an executive order strengthening the Space Force responsibility for protecting American space assets and developing capabilities to attack adversaries systems. Satellites remain crucial for modern military operations, supporting communications, surveillance, and navigation in an increasingly contested orbital domain. The public acknowledgment of orbital weapons signals a major shift in military space policy, aimed at deterring adversaries and protecting critical satellite assets.
stories.stakes: The public acknowledgment of orbital weapons signals a major shift in military space policy, aimed at deterring adversaries and protecting critical satellite assets.

stories.title: Pidcock and Backstedt lead GB at Road Worlds
stories.summary: Tom Pidcock and Zoe Backstedt will lead Great Britain at the twenty twenty-six Road World Championships in Montreal, Canada. The championships take place from September twentieth to September twenty-seventh and will be broadcast live across B B C platforms, including i Player and the B B C Sport website and app, with specific coverage on B B C Two and B B C Three. Great Britain men have a strong chance to win because Tadej Pogacar is forced to sit out the rest of the season after suffering multiple injuries in a crash at the Vuelta a Espana. Pogacar had dominated the world road race by winning in twenty twenty-four and twenty twenty-five. Ethan Hayter and Callum Thornley will compete in the men's time trial alongside defending champion Remco Evenepoel of Belgium. Hayter previously came second in the opening time trial of the Vuelta a Espana, losing to Pogacar by nine hundredths of a second. Zoe Backstedt steps up to the elite category after winning last year's Under-twenty-three race and joins a squad that also features Anna Henderson, who won silver in the time trial at the Paris Olympics in twenty twenty-four, and Anna Morris, who is thirty-one. British Cycling performance director Stephen Park said the Road World Championships are always one of the standout events in the cycling calendar and that this squad showcases the very best of British road racing. The absence of Tadej Pogacar improves Great Britain's medal prospects at the twenty twenty-six championships in Montreal. The event includes road race and time trial disciplines, with time trials featuring riders setting off at one-minute intervals.
stories.stakes: The absence of Tadej Pogacar improves Great Britain's medal prospects at the twenty twenty-six championships in Montreal.

Ethan Hayter and Callum Thornley compete in the men's time trial against defending champion Remco Evenepoel.

stories.title: Bangladesh court sentences 7 Hasina allies to death
stories.summary: A Bangladesh court on Tuesday sentenced seven senior allies of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to death in absentia. Dw Top reports the seven former Awami League officials were convicted of crimes against humanity for inciting killings during the twenty twenty-four protests. Prosecutor Mohammad Aminul Islam welcomed the verdict by saying most of the charges had been proven beyond reasonable doubt. The court also ordered the seizure of half of the defendants assets to provide compensation to families of victims. The United Nations estimates that as many as one thousand four hundred people were killed during the unrest in July and August twenty twenty-four. Sheikh Hasina was herself convicted of crimes against humanity in November twenty twenty-five and sentenced to death in absentia for her role in the crackdown. Tuesday verdict brings the total number of people convicted in trials connected with the twenty twenty-four uprising to sixty-eight. The death sentences and asset seizures for senior allies further destabilize the Awami League while the United Nations tracks accountability for the uprising. State-appointed defence lawyer M Hasan Imam noted that the seven men were not directly involved in the killings and that a lesser sentence could have been issued.
stories.stakes: The death sentences and asset seizures for senior allies further destabilize the Awami League while the United Nations tracks accountability for the uprising.
key_points: Seven senior allies of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina were sentenced to death in absentia by a Dhaka tribunal for crimes against humanity during the twenty twenty-four uprising.
The United Nations estimates that up to one thousand four hundred people were killed during the unrest in July and August twenty twenty-four.
The court ordered the seizure of half of the assets belonging to five of the defendants to compensate families of the deceased and injured.
State-appointed defence lawyer M Hasan Imam stated that the men were not directly involved in the killings and that the court could have handed down a lesser sentence.
Sheikh Hasina was previously sentenced to death in absentia in November twenty twenty-five and is currently living in exile in India.
Sixty-eight people have now been convicted in cases related to the crackdown, with twenty-two receiving death sentences and only four currently in custody.

stories.title: LSD could be approved for anxiety in the US in 2027
stories.summary:
Lysergic acid diethylamide could potentially gain U. S. Food and Drug Administration approval for treating anxiety as soon as twenty twenty-seven. This expectation follows a landmark clinical trial, according to New Scientist, showing that a single dose eased the mental health condition without severe or lasting side effects. Potential approval of the drug sets a regulatory precedent for psychiatric treatments in the United Kingdom and Europe.

Greg Cooper at University College London described the development as a milestone for psychiatric treatment. The trial recruited more than two hundred adults across the United States with moderate or severe generalised anxiety disorder. Participants assigned to take a one hundred microgram dose of the drug experienced a nine point eight point reduction in their anxiety levels after three months. That compares to a four point seven point drop in the placebo group. Robert Barrow at Definium Therapeutics noted that in a disorder with high unmet need, a single dose has shown a rapid and durable effect. Cooper emphasized that the results do not mean the drug is safe or effective to try at home. An episode can last for six to twelve hours and cause intense fear or panic. Participants were screened extremely carefully and given the drugs in a controlled environment. Unlike most psychedelic trials, participants were not offered ongoing psychotherapy, helping researchers isolate the drug-only effect.
stories.author: Carissa Wong
stories.stakes: Potential approval of the drug sets a regulatory precedent for psychiatric treatments in the United Kingdom and Europe.

stories.title: SCOTUS rejects Trump's mail voting limits. And, the Kennedy Center financial crisis
stories.summary: Senator Bernie Sanders and former strategist Steve Bannon joined forces at the Pro-Human Assembly in Washington, D. C., to address concerns about artificial intelligence. The Supreme Court blocked efforts to impose new mail-in voting restrictions before the midterm elections, ensuring the U. S. Postal Service will continue delivering ballots as usual, Npr News reports. Voting by mail has already started in states like Alabama, North Carolina, and Wisconsin. The Kennedy Center board says the arts institution faces bankruptcy and might close as soon as today, with a status hearing set by Judge Christopher Cooper overseeing a lawsuit from Representative Joyce Beatty seeking to halt the center renaming to honor Trump. Matthew Rhys pulled off a double play at the Emmys by winning lead actor in the limited series category for The Beast in Me and in the comedy series category for Widow's Bay, making him the first actor to ever win lead performance awards in two different categories in the same year. The Justice Department is investigating Evanston, Illinois, accusing it of racial discrimination over its reparations program. Costume and fashion designer Bob Mackie died of pneumonia in Palm Springs, California, on Monday at age eighty-seven. Mitch McConnell returned to the Senate yesterday after a months-long medical absence stemming from a fall. The administration is repealing limits on greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuel-fired power plants, eliminating Environmental Protection Agency rules from the prior administration.
stories.author: Brittney Melton

stories.title: Japan considers boosting defense spending to 3.5% of GDP
stories.summary:
Japan is reportedly considering boosting its defense spending to three point five percent of gross domestic product. Semafor reports that the proposed defense spending increase responds to pressure from Washington amid rising East Asia tensions. The Trump administration has pushed Tokyo to reduce its support reliance, a move that has rattled policymakers and sparked worries about shifting United States commitments. Boosting defense spending to three point five percent of gross domestic product shifts Japan toward a more self-reliant security posture amid regional tensions.

Amid changing attitudes, voters in Okinawa recently ousted a governor who opposed Tokyo militarization. Seventy percent of the nation's United States military presence is located there. Some Japanese policymakers have begun to reconsider the country's long-standing ban on nuclear weapons. This military build-up and strategic shift aim to strengthen national security and respond directly to evolving geopolitical pressures across the region.
stories.author: Jeronimo Gonzalez
stories.stakes: Boosting defense spending to three point five percent of gross domestic product shifts Japan toward a more self-reliant security posture amid regional tensions.

stories.title: Air pollution spiked after the Trump administration stopped embassy monitoring
stories.summary: In March twenty twenty-five, the Trump administration shuttered the embassy air quality monitoring program citing monetary costs. Researchers reported Monday in the journal P. N. A. S. that air pollution levels increased by twenty-four to thirty-three percent over several months following the shutdown, Npr News reports. Eric Zou says that in two thousand and eight, US officials installed an air quality monitor on the embassy in Beijing and began making information public. Zoe Yiyuan Zhou and colleagues compared air pollution levels before and after monitoring ceased across forty-six cities using satellite data. Satellite measurements translate to about a four percent increase in P. M. two point five, which are small particles entering lungs and causing health problems. The pollution increase was highest in Southeast Asian cities including Manila in the Philippines, Rangoon in Myanmar and Vientiane in Laos. Andrea La Nauze stated that the program led to sustained improvements in air quality that were continuing to increase after ten years. Zoe Yiyuan Zhou stated that having access to information is necessary to make sure that these previous gains can continue. Public information creates accountability according to researchers studying the sudden falloff of surveillance. When industries find it costs money to cut down on pollution, companies may see a lack of monitoring as an opportunity to cut those costs. The State Department did not respond to a request for comment in time for publication regarding the shutdown of more than eighty embassy and consulate monitors. Ending embassy air quality monitoring increased pollution by up to thirty-three percent across foreign cities, raising health costs for local populations.
stories.author: Jonathan Lambert
stories.stakes: Ending embassy air quality monitoring increased pollution by up to thirty-three percent across foreign cities, raising health costs for local populations.

stories.title: US Supreme Court rejects Trump’s plans on postal ballots: Why it matters
stories.summary:
The United States Supreme Court has rejected Donald Trump's bid to restrict voting by mail ahead of the November midterm elections. The ruling on Monday by the conservative supermajority court allows states to continue sending out mail ballots as they have done for years, according to Aljazeera.

In March twenty twenty-six, Trump signed an executive order directing the United States Postal Service to take control of mail voting. United States District Judge Indira Talwani imposed an injunction against the rule in June on the basis that it likely violated the United States Constitution. The Supreme Court refused to lift Judge Talwani's injunction in its latest and final decision, noting the administration was likely to fail. Justice Brett Kavanaugh voted with the majority against the administration, while Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented. The Supreme Court decision preserves mail voting procedures, protecting turnout as mail ballots account for a third of all votes cast. Mail ballots have been found to increase voter turnout. Critics have long warned that restricting mail-in ballots could disrupt the delivery of mailed votes as states have begun sending in midterm ballots. Eight states and the District of Columbia allow all elections to be conducted entirely by mail.
stories.stakes: The Supreme Court decision preserves mail voting procedures, protecting turnout as mail ballots account for a third of all votes cast.

stories.title: NATO jets shoot down a drone in Lithuanian airspace
stories.summary:
N. A. T. O. fighter jets shot down a drone that entered Lithuanian airspace overnight on Tuesday. This marks the first time that a drone has been shot down in this airspace. Military officials in Lithuania stated that the incident needed further investigation. The drone was downed near the village of Pratkūnai about sixty miles west of the capital city of Vilnius. The wreckage has been found and the drone was likely carrying explosives according to the Lithuanian air force commander, Antanas Matutis. The drone most likely entered from Belarus and remained in Lithuanian airspace for about thirty minutes. Officials in countries including Germany, Denmark, the United Kingdom, and Poland have accused Russia of involvement in recent sabotage and drone incursions. The drone interception escalates regional security tensions as European officials increasingly accuse Russia of reckless sabotage operations.

Meanwhile, Ukraine's parliament voted to dismiss Ruslan Kravchenko from the post of prosecutor general on Tuesday. A series of graft investigations has pushed tensions in Kyiv to a new high. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy suspended Kravchenko from the post just one day earlier. Various corruption scandals have hurt the approval ratings of Zelenskyy during this ongoing military conflict.
stories.author: The Associated Press
stories.stakes: The drone interception escalates regional security tensions as European officials increasingly accuse Russia of reckless sabotage operations.

stories.title: For thousands of Haitians in the U.S., end of protected status brings fear, grief and defiance
stories.summary:
Nearly three hundred fifty thousand Haitian migrants lost their temporary protected status in July after the Trump Administration revoked the designation that had shielded them from deportation for sixteen years, N. P. R. News reports. A registered nurse named Herlain barely leaves her house in Florida and told the network you would think I was on the run. Who am I on the run from. This is crazy. A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson defended the decision in an emailed statement stating that temporary protected status is exactly that temporary and that for too long it functioned as a de facto amnesty program.

Father Reginald Jean-Mary, a reverend at Notre Dame d Haiti Catholic Church in Miami, said depression and anxiety are rampant among parishioners facing deportation to Haiti, where heavily armed gangs have taken over the capital and dozens of people were recently massacred. The South Florida community was also shaken by the death of twenty-year-old Pierre Damas Bel in Springfield, Ohio, who apparently died by suicide after losing his temporary protected status and being outfitted with an ankle monitor. Little Haiti has largely emptied out with closed shops and metal shutters down because people are afraid of deportation flights and Immigration and Customs Enforcement detentions. Former broadcaster Farah Larreux, who lost her temporary protected status, said going back to Haiti would be a death sentence due to her political criticisms, and she wants another legal pathway for immigrants who fled violence and instability. Larreux pointed out the hypocrisy of the administration deporting Haitians while its State Department warns United States citizens not to travel to Haiti because it is too dangerous. The revocation of protected status for three hundred fifty thousand migrants disrupts local workforces and shuttered businesses across South Florida communities.
stories.author: Sergio Martínez-Beltrán
stories.stakes: The revocation of protected status for three hundred fifty thousand migrants disrupts local workforces and shuttered businesses across South Florida communities.

stories.title: French labour strike reduces capacity at key Dunkirk gas terminal
stories.summary:
A twenty-four-hour labor strike on Tuesday reduced delivery capacity at the Dunkirk L. N. G. terminal to four gigawatt-hours per day. The terminal normally delivers a minimum of nine point four gigawatt-hours per day, France 24 Top reports using data from Fluxys. Industrial action was expected to reduce French electricity supply by up to five gigawatts on Tuesday, while taking six point five gigawatts offline overnight on Monday. Energy sector unions staged the strike to protest recommendations from the French Court of Auditors to curb employee benefits such as access to cheaper power. The labor strike restricts gas supply at Dunkirk while Europe scrambles to refill storage ahead of winter.

The disruption is likely to affect sendout ability only, as no cargoes were scheduled to arrive at Dunkirk, according to L. S. E. G. analyst Dzmitry Dauhalevich. Elengy confirmed no disruptions occurred at the Fos or Montoir terminals.
stories.author: FRANCE 24
stories.stakes: The labor strike restricts gas supply at Dunkirk while Europe scrambles to refill storage ahead of winter.

stories.title: China tightens travel restrictions for citizens
stories.summary: China has implemented sweeping new travel rules to give the government greater control over its citizens and to prevent cutting-edge technology and top-flight researchers from leaving. Senior civil servants and executives at state-owned enterprises have long faced international travel limits. The latest rules, announced in July, target export-control and tech-sales violations. They apply to a broader swathe of private citizens and lower-level officials working in sensitive areas. Under the regulations, citizens deemed to have harmed national security or interests while overseas can be barred from leaving China for up to three years. Bbc World reports that the law also applies to anyone considered a threat to industrial or technological security. In March, co-founders of an artificial intelligence company named Manus, acquired by Meta, were reportedly barred from leaving China. Border officials must now advise Chinese nationals against traveling to high-risk regions. Official data shows court database records mentioning exit bans surged from eighty-nine in twenty-sixteen to one hundred eighty-eight thousand seven hundred sixty last year. The percentage of civil verdicts dealing with exit bans surged more than thirty times between twenty-one and twenty-five, moving from zero point two three percent to seven point three percent. A Chinese government rumor refuting platform named Piyao posted a statement last week asserting the rules do not restrict ordinary citizens, but serve as preventative measures against high-risk destinations and unusual travel patterns. Conversely, Professor Tom Kellogg of Georgetown University described the restrictions as deeply concerning and reflective of growing ideological control under Chinese leader Xi Jinping. An expert told the Financial Times that the approach keeps people and capital firmly within the party-state's control. The restrictions also increase operational risks for multinational technology companies relying on talent inside China.
stories.stakes: The expanded travel restrictions increase operational risks for multinational technology companies relying on talent and research teams based inside China.
key_points: China announced new rules in July to target export-control and tech-sales violations.
The rules apply to private citizens and lower-level officials working in sensitive areas.
Senior civil servants and state-owned enterprise executives have long faced travel limits.
Bbc World reports the law applies to anyone considered a threat to industrial or technological security.
China's supreme court database records for exit bans surged to one hundred eighty-eight thousand seven hundred sixty last year.
The Piyao platform stated the rules do not restrict ordinary citizens, but target high-risk destinations and unusual travel patterns.
Professor Tom Kellogg stated the restrictions reflect growing ideological control under leader Xi Jinping.
An expert told the Financial Times that the approach keeps people and capital within the party-state's sphere of control.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak in DRC has peaked, say authorities, as infection rates slow
stories.summary: Authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo announced that the Ebola outbreak ravaging parts of the country has reached its peak. For the first time since the epidemic was declared in May, the number of new infections is slowing down. Guardian World reports this development, noting a decline in transmission of the dangerous Bundibugyo variant. Congolese health minister, Samuel Roger Kamba, said the outbreak is now under control. At one point, health workers were recording about one hundred twenty cases per day. Today, officials are seeing about eighty cases per day. Confirmed cases stood at more than seven thousand two hundred, including more than three thousand four hundred seventy-five deaths, as of September fourteenth. The outbreak began on May fifteenth and is concentrated primarily in Ituri province. The country received more than seventy thousand doses of the Ervebo vaccine last month. Resident Léa Munyere expressed relief that people can now get back to their normal lives. One member of parliament warned against triumphalism and called for transparency in the data. Jean Kaseya previously noted that containment and contact tracing were still not effective enough. Strict adherence to preventive measures remains in place across the affected regions. The declining transmission rate of the Bundibugyo virus eases public health pressure across the affected provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
stories.author: Prosper Heri Ngorora in Goma
stories.stakes: The declining transmission rate of the Bundibugyo virus eases public health pressure across the affected provinces in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

stories.title: Alex Bores launches $30 million effort to unify Dems on AI
stories.summary: New York Assemblymember Alex Bores is launching a thirty million dollar effort called Who Decides to unite Democrats around regulating artificial intelligence. Bores is launching the new organization with his former chief of staff Anna Myers, Politico reports. The group aims by twenty twenty-eight to have Democratic candidates run with a common A. I. safety agenda. The agenda addresses current harms and broader dangers that increasingly powerful systems could destabilize the economy, democracy, and safety. The new political organization aims to unite Democrats around a common safety agenda to regulate frontier artificial intelligence by twenty twenty-eight. Who Decides will reject corporate money or contributions from senior executives at frontier A. I. companies. The initiative will conduct quarterly national and state polls, host national conferences, and partner with local groups in those states. The launch follows a failed congressional campaign earlier this year where Bores gained national attention for his opposition to unchecked artificial intelligence.
stories.author: By Jason Beeferman
stories.stakes: The new political organization aims to unite Democrats around a common safety agenda to regulate frontier artificial intelligence by twenty twenty-eight.

stories.title: AI regulation faces political deadlock as calls grow for Congress to act
stories.summary: President Donald Trump wrote on social media that artificial intelligence taking over the world is a hoax. Democratic House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries told reporters that Congress should not leave town until A. I. safety is addressed, according to Bbc World. Republican Speaker Mike Johnson gave no sign that he intended to move quickly on A. I. legislation before the upcoming House recess. Republican Senate Majority Leader John Thune and democratic senator Amy Klobuchar are working on a bill to force federal oversight on some A. I. companies. Democratic congresswoman Lori Trahan worked on a bipartisan House proposal called the Frontier Act requiring independent audits of A. I. research labs. Trump top A. I. adviser David Sacks told C. B. S. News that existential warnings about artificial intelligence have been overblown and are becoming a panic. Partisan division over artificial intelligence safety legislation in Congress stalls federal oversight for companies developing advanced frontier models.
stories.stakes: Partisan division over artificial intelligence safety legislation in Congress stalls federal oversight for companies developing advanced frontier models.

stories.title: Hyrox changes rules and apologises for allowing Australian athlete who soiled herself to continue
stories.summary: Fitness competition organisers have issued an apology and implemented immediate rule changes after an incident in Beijing. During the event, Guardian Sport reports that an Australian participant was allowed to finish and win despite soiling herself mid-race. Footage showed world record holder Joanna Wietrzyk continuing through demanding exercises and using communal equipment while visibly soiled. This sparked widespread debate regarding health and safety standards. Hyrox co-founder Moritz Fürste addressed the situation in an Instagram statement. He said that Hyrox made a mistake by failing to react immediately during the event and added that new procedures are now in place. Organisers from Hyrox China and Hyrox World confirmed that affected lanes were isolated for overnight deep cleaning. Contaminated equipment was removed, and venue carpets were replaced before competition resumed. The incident raised concerns among participants who paid to compete. Competitor Joe Ho noted that exposed athletes faced potential physical and psychological consequences and deserved meaningful compensation. Following online backlash targeting Wietrzyk, organisers issued a warning that individuals sending abuse or threats of violence toward the athlete will face bans from all future events. Fitness competition organisers face growing pressure to protect health standards and competitor welfare after hygiene failures during international racing events.
stories.author: Ima Caldwell
stories.stakes: Fitness competition organisers face growing pressure to protect health standards and competitor welfare after hygiene failures during international racing events.

stories.title: Elementic’s MO6 is the building material claiming to lock away carbon for thousands of years
stories.summary: A Finnish materials startup named Elementic created an innovative wall surfacing tile called M. O. six. Optimist Daily reports that the product is ninety percent carbon by chemistry and stores approximately two point four kilograms of atmospheric carbon dioxide for every kilogram of material used. Unlike traditional wood that eventually burns or decays, this material does not decay. Elementic general manager Johanna Normiala described the production method by stating we take the lignin, we create a kind of dough that we bake like a cake, and in the end we get a hard, resistant, durable material but which is lightweight. The company launched its debut collection named M. O. six Eternal on September second at the Habitare design trade fair in Helsinki as part of Helsinki Design Week. Elementic is intentionally positioning the product as a premium interior design brand to reach architects, hotel developers, and interior designers. A spa currently under construction in Paris is among the first named examples receiving the delivered product. The company expects further manufacturing improvements and plans to eventually develop bricks for broader construction applications. The permanent carbon storage product provides architects and developers a recyclable premium material that locks away emissions indefinitely.
stories.author: The Optimist Editorial Team
stories.stakes: The permanent carbon storage product provides architects and developers a recyclable premium material that locks away emissions indefinitely.

stories.title: Telus Warns Customers of Account Breaches
stories.summary: Telus is notifying customers that their accounts have been breached. The data intrusions on these accounts occurred between February twenty twenty-five and June twenty twenty-six, according to Tldr Infosec. Attackers used compromised credentials to access stored personal information like names and account numbers and phone numbers. The obtained information was used to attempt convincing customers to move their services to competitors, and attackers made unauthorized changes to victim services in some cases. Telus has reset the compromised credentials and added enhanced security monitoring to impacted accounts. The Vancouver Police Department has been notified about the account breaches, and victims have been offered complimentary identity theft protection services. It remains unclear how many total accounts were affected by the unauthorized access campaign.
stories.author: TLDR
stories.stakes: The breach exposes telecom customer data over a sixteen month period, forcing security resets and police investigations.

stories.title: Bending Spoons to Acquire Miro for $1.36 Billion in All-Cash Deal as Tech Buying Spree Accelerates
stories.summary: Bending Spoons is acquiring workplace collaboration platform Miro in a one point three six billion dollar all cash deal announced Thursday. Tldr Design reports that the transaction carries an enterprise value of one point three five five billion dollars, while Miro net cash brings the implied equity value to roughly one point seven nine billion dollars. Some Miro shareholders have agreed to reinvest two hundred ninety-five million dollars of their proceeds into newly issued Bending Spoons equity. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of twenty twenty-six pending regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. Miro has around six hundred million dollars in annual recurring revenue, with nearly ninety percent coming from business and enterprise customers across more than two hundred fifty thousand organizations. Bending Spoons chief executive officer and co-founder, Luca Ferrari stated, It is a privilege and no small responsibility to welcome a product that over two hundred fifty thousand organizations have integrated into their workflows. Miro chief executive officer and co-founder, Andrey Khusid noted, We started Miro fifteen years ago to give teams one place to think together and bring ideas to life. Bending Spoons continues its aggressive tech buying spree that already includes Airtable, Vimeo, Evernote, Eventbrite, A. O. L., Brightcove, and WeTransfer, building an unusual portfolio of widely known software brands. The billion dollar acquisition expands Bending Spoons into enterprise collaboration software, adding a quarter million corporate clients to their tech portfolio.
stories.author: TLDR
stories.stakes: The billion dollar acquisition expands Bending Spoons into enterprise collaboration software, adding a quarter million corporate clients to their tech portfolio.

stories.title: For the first time, the US military confirms it has deployed weapons in orbit
stories.summary: The United States has confirmed for the first time that it has deployed a space weapon in Earth orbit. Air Force Secretary Troy Meink made the declaration on Monday at the Air and Space Cyber Conference near Washington, D. C. According to the official Air Force account, Meink stated the weapon is necessary to safeguard joint forces against evolving adversary threats, artificial intelligence, and autonomous weapons. He declined to reveal specific details or testing timelines, noting that discussing such specifics would not benefit deterrence. A U S Space Force spokesperson stated that space control involves kinetic and non-kinetic means for offensive and defensive purposes, including disruption and destruction. Senior military leaders previously cited Russian and Chinese programmes designed to disrupt U S satellites. China responded on Tuesday by warning against an arms race in outer space. Dr Bleddyn Bowen from the R U S I stated the technology could involve electronic warfare, radio jamming, or a kinetic kill vehicle, though a kinetic weapon is less likely due to debris risks. Juliana Suess at the German Institute of International and Security Affairs noted the weaponry is based in space rather than being an Earth-based missile. Victoria Samson from the Secure World Foundation called the statement very destabilizing and noted it is meant to solidify the U S Space Force as a warfighting branch. Meink also stated the U S needs to increase combat power faster and more affordably, aiming for a radically different-looking Air Force by twenty thirty-two, while highlighting how the conflict in Ukraine has shifted warfare toward autonomous systems and drones. The Trump administration previously included space capabilities in its planned Golden Dome defense system. Donald Trump issued an executive order last year highlighting the U S Space Force's role as an attacking force. Launched in twenty nineteen, the U S Space Force is the first new branch of the U S military in over seventy years. A nineteen sixty-seven treaty banned weapons of mass destruction in orbit. This prompted powers to explore other capabilities outside the treaty. In twenty twenty-four, the U S stated Russia launched a satellite believed capable of attacking other probes. The U S Space Force states that China and Russia view space as a warfighting domain.
stories.author: TLDR
stories.stakes: Placing space control weapons in orbit provides the United States military with essential capabilities to defend joint forces against evolving adversary threats.
key_points: The United States confirmed for the first time that it has deployed a space weapon in Earth orbit.
Air Force Secretary Troy Meink announced the deployment at the Air and Space Cyber Conference on Monday.
Meink declined to reveal specific details or testing timelines to protect deterrence.
Juliana Suess noted the weapon is based in space and ranges from jamming to kinetic effects.
Victoria Samson called the statement very destabilizing and said it solidifies the U S Space Force as a warfighting branch.
China responded on Tuesday by warning against an arms race in space.
Meink stated the U S will have a radically different-looking Air Force by twenty thirty-two using autonomous systems.

stories.title: ENISA launches Single Reporting Platform as EU Cyber Resilience Act vulnerability reporting obligations take effect
stories.summary: The E. U. Agency for Cybersecurity deployed the initial operating capability of the Single Reporting Platform. Tldr Infosec reports that the online tool was developed to enable manufacturers to meet their new Cyber Resilience Act reporting obligations for actively exploited vulnerabilities. The platform allows users to report once and communicate relevant information to all appropriate authorities. The framework supports a coordinated approach to vulnerability reporting across the European Union and builds a more resilient Digital Single Market. The new reporting platform standardizes vulnerability disclosures for European Union software manufacturers, altering compliance obligations across member states ahead of mandatory deadlines. From September eleventh twenty twenty-six, manufacturers are required to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents having an impact on security. These obligations also apply to open source software stewards involved in developing products with digital elements. Main cybersecurity requirements apply from December eleventh twenty twenty-seven.
stories.author: TLDR
stories.stakes: The new reporting platform standardizes vulnerability disclosures for European Union software manufacturers, altering compliance obligations across member states ahead of mandatory deadlines.

stories.title: Hochul’s how-to guide to stopping ICE
stories.summary: Governor Kathy Hochul sent a letter to local government leaders explaining legal barriers to halt Immigration and Customs Enforcement efforts in their communities. Federal immigration officials confirmed an acquisition is underway to lease a new facility for enforcement and removal operations in the Hudson Valley. Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg announced his office seized a dozen domains used to create, disseminate, and sell artificial intelligence deepfake pornography, according to Politico. The seized websites featured artificial intelligence-generated images and videos of roughly twelve hundred individuals engaging in sexually explicit activity. Bragg stated that horrific violations of privacy follow victims into their careers and personal lives. In education news, the high school class of twenty twenty-seven will be the final group required to pass state Regents exams to graduate. State education officials announced that beginning with students graduating in twenty twenty-eight, Regents exams will become optional rather than mandatory for high school graduation.
stories.author: By Nick Reisman and Joe Anuta
stories.stakes: The phase out of mandatory Regents exams for the class of twenty twenty-eight alters graduation standards for New York high school students.

stories.title: OpenAI buys smartphone camera maker Glass Imaging for $300 million, report says
stories.summary: OpenAI acquired smartphone camera maker Glass Imaging in a deal worth over three hundred million dollars, Techcrunch reports. Founded in twenty nineteen in Los Altos, California, Glass Imaging was created by former Apple engineers Ziv Attar and Tom Bishop. The startup had previously raised about thirty million dollars in funding from investors. Rather than editing photos after capture, Glass Imaging uses neural networks to overcome physical camera constraints and yield better images the moment the shutter clicks. The ChatGPT maker is rumored to be working on its own hardware devices like smartphones, earbuds, and A. I. companion devices. Previously in twenty twenty-five, OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman and designer Jony Ive revealed they were working together on a device startup called io when OpenAI bought Ive company for six point five billion dollars. OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding the latest acquisition. The acquisition accelerates hardware development for the artificial intelligence company as it builds competing consumer devices.
stories.author: Amanda Silberling
stories.stakes: The acquisition accelerates hardware development for the artificial intelligence company as it builds competing consumer devices.

stories.title: AI infrastructure company Cornelis raises $205M to chip away at Nvidia’s dominance
stories.summary: Artificial intelligence infrastructure company Cornelis announced on Monday that it has raised two hundred five million dollars in a funding round led by I. A. G. Capital Partners. Techcrunch reports that the company also unveiled a product named Active Compute Fabric. This network technology addresses the issue of graphical processing unit time wasted waiting for data by allowing chips to process and send information simultaneously. While Nvidia remains dominant and optimized for its own software stack, Cornelis is part of a new wave of infrastructure firms working to break that dominance chip by chip. Cornelis has already started shipping its current product and expects to release a new generation of the technology later this year, challenging Nvidia's market dominance by securing two hundred five million dollars to scale its new networking technology.
stories.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
stories.stakes: Cornelis challenges Nvidia's market dominance by securing two hundred five million dollars to scale its new networking technology.

stories.title: New Crops, Health Research Proposals to Help NASA Advance Exploration
stories.summary: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration has selected twelve new investigations to support human explorers in space. Nasa Breaking reports that six of these projects advance food production off planet using Space Crops grants. Four space crops proposals study edible plants and how environmental conditions affect their growth in space or on other planets. Another proposal examines resurrection plants and how they withstand extreme dry conditions. The final space crops proposal uncovers functions of algal genes modified by spaceflight. A second set of six proposals focuses on precision health and how space exploration affects well being. These include studies on lunar dust impacts on respiratory and immune responses alongside repurposed drugs to mitigate health effects. Two more proposals look at how radiation combined with other stressors affects age relevant characteristics across various systems. The agency will award more than seven million dollars in grant money throughout fiscal years twenty twenty-six through twenty thirty. Principal investigators come from ten institutions across eight states with nine awards going to first time recipients. The seven million dollar research investment advances life support systems and health countermeasures needed for long duration human space exploration.
stories.stakes: The seven million dollar research investment advances life support systems and health countermeasures needed for long duration human space exploration.

stories.title: Athens Is Turning its Old Airport into One of Europe’s Largest Parks
stories.summary: A former Athens airport site is transforming into the Ellinikon Park. It will stretch over four hundred acres along the sea in a southern suburb, according to Good News Network. Planners designed the space to serve as a shaded refuge for residents of Europe is hottest city. The project aims to keep the park seven point two degrees Fahrenheit cooler than surrounding asphalt and concrete areas. To achieve this thermoregulation, the park will feature thirty thousand trees and three million smaller plants representing more than five hundred twenty species of flora. Rest areas will offer a shading ratio of more than sixty percent, while water features include running channels and misting systems. Athens previously held the World Meteorological Organization record for the highest temperature ever recorded in Europe at forty-eight point zero degrees Celsius. In twenty twenty-four, under the mayorship of Haris Doukas, the city began planting its first micro-forest alongside greening projects across six neighborhoods. The Ellinikon Park will utilize onsite water treatment facilities and a giant rainwater catchment system to support its flora. The park is planned to open to the public next year, with future renovations scheduled for twenty thirty. The urban cooling project sets a municipal climate adaptation precedent for dense southern European cities facing rising summer temperatures.
stories.author: Andy Corbley
stories.stakes: The urban cooling project sets a municipal climate adaptation precedent for dense southern European cities facing rising summer temperatures.

stories.title: New York Seizes a Dozen Celebrity Deepfake Websites
stories.summary: The Manhattan District Attorney Office seized twelve domains used for selling celebrity deepfakes.
