Built from lessons learned over eight years of running large sharded M y S Q L clusters.
Each Neki shard is a full Postgres cluster featuring one primary and at least two replicas across three availability zones.
Routers feature a full Postgres query parser, a distributed query planner, and query buffering, and can scale vertically and horizontally.
Sidecars run alongside every Postgres instance to improve connection handling and pool sizing.
Data topology is a JSON configuration that uses shard indexes and shard groups to map logical tables to physical shards.
Workflows switch traffic using a double underscore neki metafunction over a p s q l connection.
Planet Scale warns users not to run production workloads on Neki during the platform preview because breaking changes are expected.

stories.title: TSMC's August revenue jumps 53% to a record high, plans High-NA EUV adoption for 2030
stories.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company reported record monthly revenue for August. Strong demand for artificial intelligence chips drove the growth. A. I. is the acronym for artificial intelligence. The world's largest contract chipmaker posted revenue of five hundred fourteen point eight billion New Taiwan dollars. That is equivalent to sixteen point three five billion dollars. This marks a fifty-three point three percent increase from a year earlier. It is also a ten point one percent jump from July. The company stated that A. I. related demand continued to be extremely robust during its July earnings call. This follows a second-quarter profit increase of more than seventy-seven percent. It marks the fourth consecutive month of rising monthly revenue. TrendForce data released Wednesday showed the company maintained a seventy-two point five percent market share in the global foundry market during the second quarter. Samsung Foundry ranked second with five point nine percent. China's S. M. I. C. followed with five point four percent. Strong demand for A. I. server processors kept advanced five, four, and three nanometer capacity fully booked through the quarter. The company and A. S. M. L. announced an initiative to advance next-generation chipmaking technology. The company plans to use High N. A. technology in large-scale manufacturing starting in twenty thirty. A. I. applications increasingly demand more complex transistor architectures.
stories.author: TLDR

stories.title: Lawsuit challenges intimidation of DHS observers across the country
stories.summary:
A new federal lawsuit challenges what it calls a nationwide policy of intimidation and retaliation. The complaint was filed on Thursday in Washington, D. C.

Minneapolis resident Michael Khalili and the nonprofit Common Cause brought the action. They filed the ninety-four-page complaint against the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Justice, the F. B. I., and other agencies.

The lawsuit accuses the federal government of violating the First Amendment and privacy rights. This affects observers in Maryland, Minnesota, New Jersey, Illinois, Maine, and Tennessee.

The legal action asks a judge for national relief. It wants to bar federal agencies from intimidating or retaliating against legal observers.

The complaint outlines encounters faced by seven Common Cause members and other activists. They were photographed, followed, pepper-sprayed, and threatened with police visits. They were also subjected to facial recognition databases, administrative subpoenas, and the revocation of trusted traveler statuses like Global Entry.

The complaint highlights the case of Michael Khalili. He is a forty-seven-year-old father of two. He stopped observing Immigration and Customs Enforcement following pressure from his family and tense exchanges with federal officers.

Law enforcement queried his state motor vehicle records fifty-five times since March of twenty twenty-six. That compares to just twice before he began observing. His Global Entry status was revoked one day after an encounter with immigration officers. It was later reinstated following a journalist's inquiry.

The lawsuit argues these actions stem from top-down Trump administration directives. These include National Security Presidential Memorandum seven and associated Department of Justice memos. The directives link impeding immigration enforcement to domestic terrorism. They also repeal guardrails on facial recognition and license plate readers.

Danielle Lang is the vice president of voting rights and rule of law at the Campaign Legal Center. Her organization is litigating the case. She stated that the events described are a top-down policy of retaliation that needs to be addressed.

Maryam Jazini Dorcheh is the Common Cause vice president for litigation. She said the right of citizens to criticize and hold the government accountable is under attack. She added that criminalizing peaceful observation hinders their mission.

The Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Justice did not provide an immediate response to the allegations. The F. B. I. declined to comment.
stories.author: Jude Joffe-Block

stories.title: Anthropic caught scientists using Claude to further biological weapon research
stories.summary: Anthropic caught scientists using Claude to further biological weapon research. The company shared this new report on Thursday. The findings include five case studies of models being used to develop biological weapons. They also include safety measures and company responses. In one instance from May, Anthropic caught a flagged request. The request asked Claude to author a grant for gain-of-function research. The research focused on the chikungunya virus. That is a pathogen with no licensed treatment that causes debilitating symptoms. The proposal sought to genetically alter the virus. It aimed to increase its transmissibility and immune response evasion. The proposal originated from a military research institute. The company took similar issue with gain-of-function research into bird flu. A separate case involved a researcher using Claude for different work. The researcher built an atlas of venom toxin peptides. They also built a generative pipeline that optimized toxin characteristics. The full report includes case studies on other topics. Those topics are models being used as a surveillance tool, software exploits, propaganda, and weapons systems. Jacob Klein is Anthropic's head of threat intelligence. He told The New York Times that the situations are incredibly nuanced. He stated you do not see someone in a comic book kind of way wanting to build a biological weapon to kill everybody. Detecting misuse is complicated. Research into a new vaccine could look a lot like creating a bioweapon. This prompted Anthropic to err on the side of caution due to potential consequences. The company banned the accounts of anyone misusing Claude or Anthropic models. Anthropic is using the findings to further improve safeguards. The company is not naming the individuals or institutions involved. Anthropic noted that the implicated parties are working scientists. The company does not assert that they intended harm. Identifying them could expose them to harm.
stories.author: staff@engadget.com (Ian Carlos Campbell)

stories.title: LinkedIn beats "BrowserGate" lawsuits over scanning users' Chrome extensions
stories.summary:
LinkedIn has won the dismissal of two class-action lawsuits over scanning browser extensions. Judge Vince Chhabria granted the motion to dismiss on Tuesday. The judge said the plaintiffs failed to establish legal standing. Neither user proved they had browser extensions installed that sent private data to LinkedIn.

The judge gave the plaintiffs a chance to amend their complaints. He expressed deep skepticism about their future chances. He wrote that users voluntarily download browser extensions. These tools intentionally expose data to websites by their very nature. It seems unlikely the plaintiffs will ever prove a privacy violation.

The lawsuits were filed separately in April. Attorney J. R. Howell represents one of the plaintiffs. He is evaluating whether to refile the claims in a California state court. That court operates under different standing requirements. He is also considering an appeal in the U. S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit.
stories.author: Jon Brodkin

stories.title: Canada offers air defense support for Ukraine as Zelenskyy visits
stories.summary: Canada offered support on Thursday to boost Ukrainian air defenses during a visit by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The leaders signed an agreement to work toward a hundred-year partnership covering defense and critical minerals and energy. Carney assured,Zelenskyy that Canada will always be with you. Ukrainians helped build Canada and Canadians will help rebuild Ukraine. The announced support includes three hundred and fifty million Canadian dollars. That equals two hundred and fifty-three million United States dollars. It is provided through the United States Jumpstart program. Carney also announced four hundred and fifty million Canadian dollars in loan guarantees. These funds will enhance the Ukrainian energy supply by repairing damaged infrastructure. They will also increase storage capacity and improve power to hospitals to help Ukrainians get through the winter. Canada announced a deal that will send thirty percent of new Canadian drone production directly to Ukraine. Zelenskyy stated that these drones will go immediately to the battlefield and to soldiers to save families first of all. Zelenskyy plans to meet Donald Trump in New York City in late September.
stories.author: Agence France-Presse

stories.title: BRICS 2026: Delhi braces for traffic diversions from 2 pm to 8:30 pm tomorrow, check alternate routes, diversion points
stories.summary: Delhi commuters face extensive travel disruptions on Friday, September eleventh. Traffic regulations and diversions take effect for the B. R. I. C. S. Summit. The summit happens at Bharat Mandapam in Pragati Maidan. The restrictions operate from two p m to eight thirty p m. They impact more than thirty-five roads and twenty-two designated diversion points. These affect central and south Delhi, the airport corridors, and railway stations. The high profile summit runs from September eleventh to September thirteenth. It brings foreign delegations and very important person motorcades to the national capital. Nearly forty-eight hundred traffic personnel are deployed by Delhi Police to manage security arrangements. Non-destined commercial vehicles are barred from entering Delhi. Emergency and medical vehicles retain priority passage. Roadside parking within two hundred metres of controlled corridors is prohibited. The traffic plan lists numerous regulated routes. These include Sardar Patel Marg, Shanti Path, Akbar Road, Mathura Road, and Ashoka Road. There are twenty-two diversion points. Locations include areas around Connaught Place, Patel Chowk, Dhaula Kuan, Moti Bagh, and Lodhi Road. Traffic may be stopped at short notice during very important person movements. This creates uncertainty and congestion on connecting corridors. The Delhi Traffic Police strongly recommends using the Metro. This is particularly true for airport-bound passengers. Alternative routes are established for travellers heading to Indira Gandhi International Airport from Gurugram, Dwarka, and various parts of the city. Other routes help those commuting to New Delhi, Old Delhi, and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations.

stories.title: NASA Answers President’s Call to Establish United States Space Academy
stories.summary:
National Aeronautics and Space Administration Administrator Jared Isaacman chaired the first Presidential Commission on the United States Space Academy meeting on September ninth. The meeting followed an Executive Order signed by President Donald Trump to create the institution.

Isaacman and Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson met with key officials at National Aeronautics and Space Administration Headquarters in Washington. Those officials included United States Chief Technology Officer Ethan Klein. They discussed governance, curriculum, service commitments, and partnerships for the academy.

Responses to the Request for Information will help inform the path forward for the commission. Those responses are due by six p.m. Eastern Daylight Time on Monday, October twenty-sixth. Each state is allowed one submission through its governor designee.

The commission operates under a one hundred twenty day mandate. It must develop recommendations for President Trump to build the technical talent and leadership pipeline for America in space.

The timeline outlines groundbreaking no later than twenty twenty-seven. The academy will temporarily host the first three hundred students in twenty twenty-eight. A permanent location will be in operation by twenty thirty-one.

Isaacman shared his thoughts after the meeting. He stated that the first commission meeting made clear how much talent and commitment stand behind the vision of President Trump for the United States Space Academy.
stories.author: Lauren E. Low

stories.title: Digital data leeches: trading on our profiles
stories.summary:
About twelve thousand app users in Britain sued the dating app Grindr. They claimed the app shared sensitive personal information like H. I. V. status with advertisers. The lawsuit was filed in twenty twenty-four and was settled earlier this week. Grindr agreed to pay claimants a total of twenty-six million pounds. That equals approximately thirty million euros or thirty-five million dollars. The company stressed that the settlement is not an admission of liability. They continue to dispute the allegations and noted there has been no legal judgement.

The case highlights broader concerns about data privacy. People worry about how information entrusted to apps is handled by cloud services and advertising networks., Jan Penfrat, a digital policy expert for European Digital Rights, spoke about the issue. He stated that many big tech companies want to make tracking difficult for users and regulators. They try to hide what data is gathered on devices and for what purpose.

The European Union enforces strict rules like the General Data Protection Regulation. They also use the Digital Markets Act and the Digital Services Act. In twenty twenty-five, the E. U. Commission handed out massive fines. They fined Apple five hundred million euros, Meta two hundred million euros, and Google eight hundred ninety million euros., Jan Penfrat noted that these sums are tiny amounts. Companies like Google or Amazon make that much money in just a few days. This allows them to simply include fines in their regular budgets. Effective oversight is further complicated by other factors. Europe relies heavily on cloud services and operating systems provided by American companies. There is also a lack of political will in Brussels. Officials fail to properly equip European data protection authorities and take firmer action.

stories.title: Google Earth’s AI experiment lasted 24 hours. The damage to trust will linger
stories.summary:
Authorities and journalists turned to commercial satellite imagery to separate fact from fiction after strikes in the Gulf region in February. Google launched a new feature that built image generation directly into Google Earth on July thirty-first. Users conjured fake nuclear plants and bomb craters within hours. Rest Of World reports that Google pulled the feature after an outcry from experts and the media. The quick recall of Google Earth image generation highlights ongoing risks when deploying artificial intelligence tools into critical verification infrastructure.

OpenAI shut down its Sora video app in March following public demands. Google launched the Veo three video generator in May twenty twenty-five. Regulation has struggled to keep pace with the rapid development of artificial intelligence models. Some transparency obligations required by the European Union A. I. Act enacted in twenty twenty-four began on August second, twenty twenty-six. Detection tools remain inadequate while implementation is shaky. This environment allows bad actors to dismiss authentic evidence using the theory of the liar dividend. Expert Hany Farid noted that the loss of trust in the visual record demands mainstream solutions. No one can recall the doubt that now attaches to every image out of a war zone.
stories.author: Mahsa Alimardani
stories.stakes: The quick recall of Google Earth image generation highlights ongoing risks when deploying artificial intelligence tools into critical verification infrastructure.

stories.title: Can the US battery market untangle from China?
stories.summary: In late August, the Trump administration issued an executive order declaring a national emergency. This order effectively bans Chinese batteries from grid-scale energy storage systems, along with inverters and transformers. The United States relies on cheap Chinese batteries to rapidly grow its energy storage market and cut emissions. This follows earlier measures, including Section three hundred one tariffs that increased import taxes on batteries to twenty-five percent in January, up from seven point five percent. It also follows tax credit restrictions originating from the twenty twenty-two Inflation Reduction Act. Under upcoming legislation taking effect in twenty twenty-six, fifty-five percent of the cost of materials for new energy storage projects must come from outside China and other restricted countries for projects to qualify for tax credits. An outright ban was a surprise, and it creates concern for domestic players in the United States, according to Shan Tomouk, energy storage and energy lead for Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. BloombergNEF analysis indicates the move will likely slow deployment in the near term and cause project delays. Isshu Kikuma, an energy storage analyst at BloombergNEF, notes that in the worst case, projects could face cancellation if they cannot find alternative and more expensive sources following Department of Energy guidance expected by the end of the year. While the order technically applies to existing plants, analysts consider it unlikely they will be taken offline, as doing so would remove most installed battery storage from the grid. Longer term, the United States could reach enough domestic capacity by around twenty thirty, with support from new factories by companies including LG Energy Solutions, Samsung SDI, Ford, and SK On, though domestic supply may not fully meet demand until later in the twenty thirties as the market absorbs these higher costs.
stories.author: Casey Crownhart

stories.title: Expanding AI access and cyber defense for federal, state, local, and tribal governments
stories.summary:
OpenAI and the United States General Services Administration have announced a multi-year agreement. The deal expands artificial intelligence and cyber defense tools to federal, state, local, and tribal governments. The twenty-seven-month agreement runs from October first, twenty twenty-six, through December thirty-first, twenty twenty-eight. It extends eligibility across a public sector workforce of approximately twenty-three million people. This builds on existing agreements that already cover more than one million government employees.

The deal eliminates the standard fifteen-dollar-per-user-per-month license fee. It sets the fee to zero with no minimum commitment. It also provides fifty percent off usage costs for eligible organizations. Verified government entities will be approved for advanced cyber-defender Daybreak Blue access. This comes at fifty percent off standard commercial pricing alongside scaled training and enablement. Defenders can also request access to Daybreak Red. This tool offers advanced vulnerability research, exploit validation, and red teaming at standard commercial pricing.

Practical implementations under previous access show major successes. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention accelerated public health literature reviews to under thirty minutes. The Georgia Department of Revenue reduced tax form digitization time from two weeks to fifteen minutes. The North Carolina Department of State Treasurer identified millions of dollars in potential unclaimed property. Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory compressed months of fusion research model development into hours. OpenAI President, Greg Brockman, stated that public servants should have access to the best A. I. tools available. He noted that helping government work better by making services faster, easier, safer, and more reliable is a key way to bring the benefits of A. I. to everyone.

stories.title: Rubio signals shift to working with allies to fight drug trade as latest boat strike kills three
stories.summary:
The US Southern Command announced a strike in the Caribbean Sea late Wednesday. The attack killed three people. This brings the total death toll to at least two hundred thirty people. The total comes from sixty-nine strikes.

Public acknowledgment follows a year of unilateral deadly strikes. These strikes targeted boats operated by narco-terrorists in international waters. The campaign began in September twenty twenty-five.

Recent operations involve joint efforts unlike earlier unilateral actions. People on floating refueling stations are transferred to local authorities. Then the US military destroys the vessels.

The administration is building agreements with regional allies. These allies include Colombia and Ecuador.

Rubio spoke to reporters in Quito. He called it an incredible advance for countries to participate in efforts within their territorial waters. He noted that the important point is that these trafficking routes are being disrupted and ended.

He described the approach as a strike-by-strike or operation-by-operation determination. This depends on the threat and location of the boat. Rubio stated during a trip to Quito that the military will still blow up ships if need be.

Rubio delivered these remarks during a three-country tour of South America. The tour aimed at boosting security cooperation with conservative leaders.
stories.author: Associated Press

stories.title: NYC schools issue the country’s broadest AI ban, covering pre-K through eighth grade
stories.summary: New York City Public Schools is banning generative A. I. for pre-kindergarten through eighth grade students for the twenty twenty-six to twenty twenty-seven school year. More than half a million students are affected by the sweeping district policy, Optimist Daily reports, which is considered the nation's most expansive A. I. moratorium. High school students and teachers are exempt from the restriction. Mayor Zohran Mamdani stated that the tech industry wants everyone to believe that A. I. powered early education is necessary. Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels emphasized that the district will ensure technology serves learning rather than the other way around. The sweeping ban affects over half a million students, setting a major regulatory precedent for early artificial intelligence policy in urban public school districts. The district aims to protect foundational critical thinking skills by preventing young students from outsourcing their work to companion chatbots and software before they have built the ability to do it themselves.
stories.author: The Optimist Editorial Team
stories.stakes: The sweeping ban affects over half a million students, setting a major regulatory precedent for early artificial intelligence policy in urban public school districts.

stories.title: ClearFake WebDAV Infection Chain Delivers Amatera Stealer, ZigCryptoStealer, and NetSupport Manager
stories.summary:
Researchers at Cisco Talos investigated an unusual cyber attack at a Ukrainian government organization in April twenty twenty-six. The attack used a WebDAV execution chain. A thirty-two-bit rundll32.exe process launched a remote D. L. L. named verification.google.

One branch relied on a JavaScript injection. It used a Cloudflare Worker and EtherHiding on the B. N. B. Smart Chain. Victims were tricked into executing a WebDAV path through a fake Google CAPTCHA.

The resulting loader deployed Amatera build four point one point five alpha. This build found its command-and-control server through a Telegra.ph page disguised as a Rust tutorial. The server told the build to deploy a NativeAOT loader running ZigCryptoStealer and a Go-based reverse proxy.

The verification.google branch used a D. L. L. hollowing technique in dbghelp.dll. Its infrastructure instructed it to install an unauthorized instance of NetSupport Manager using a Russia-based I. P. address.

Cisco Talos tracks the threat actor behind the verification.google activity as U. A. T. dash ten thousand eight hundred twenty. They assess with moderate confidence that the operations are part of a broader crypto and credential theft network rather than targeted attacks against specific entities.
stories.author: TLDR

stories.title: Adobe Commerce max-severity bug comes under active attack
stories.summary:
Online stores running Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source face active attacks from a zero-day vulnerability tracked as C. V. E. twenty twenty-six, seventy-five thousand six hundred fifty.

The flaw carries a critical score of ten point zero and impacts versions two point four point four through two point four point nine of both platforms.

Security firm Sansec dubbed the flaw StyleSmuggler.

Exploitation began on September fourth, with the first confirmed attack recorded at twenty-two twenty U. T. C.

The vulnerability allows attackers to inject malicious P. H. P. code by abusing template processing during failed payment email notifications.

A successful attack launches a background process.

This process is a small Rust program that connects to a command and control server.

The server address is ninety-nine point eighty-four point sixty-seven point one hundred eighty-six.

The program waits for commands and uses persistence mechanisms like cron jobs.

It disguises its traffic as network time protocol traffic over U. D. P. port one hundred twenty-three.

A separate attacker used the vulnerability to deploy a web shell inside the product-image cache on September seventh.

Adobe released an emergency hotfix tracked as V. U. L. N. dash thirty-nine thousand three hundred forty-one to close the vulnerability.

Attackers had a three-day window to exploit the flaw before the fix arrived.

Sansec warns that patching alone is insufficient for stores that may have already been compromised.

Researchers recommend checking for unexpected P. H. P. files under pub slash media.

Stores should also look for known malicious processes, cron entries, and other indicators of compromise.
stories.author: TLDR

stories.title: Google's AI genome system evaluates every possible one-base change
stories.summary: Google announced a new resource on Tuesday called AlphaGenome Atlas. It predicts the consequences of every possible single-base variant in the human genome. The system processes nine billion bases through AlphaGenome software across the human genome. The system is engineered to identify the potential functions of non-coding DNA. This non-coding material makes up the vast majority of the human genome. It does not encode proteins itself. This region does not build proteins. Portions of it are essential for controlling the activity of protein-coding regions. It instructs cells where and when to make messenger RNAs and how to process them. Much of it appears to consist of remnants from viruses and other molecular parasites. Having all this analysis performed by a single software package is useful. Being able to pinpoint functional portions of DNA is also useful. The true value of AlphaGenome will remain unclear until biologists begin heavy adoption. This adoption will show what the tool offers beyond its original training data.
stories.author: John Timmer

stories.title: Megan Eckert Just Ran 636 Miles in 6 Days—and Destroyed the Overall American Record
stories.summary: Megan Eckert ran six hundred thirty-six point four eight two miles in six days at the G. O. M. U. six-day World Championships in Hungary. Runnersworld News reports that the forty-year-old teacher from Santa Fe, New Mexico, was the overall winner of the event after completing one thousand one hundred forty laps around a zero point five five eight one-mile loop. By averaging one hundred six miles per day, she shattered the overall American record of six hundred six point two four three miles set by Joe Fejes in twenty fifteen. Eckert also surpassed the womens three-day world record by logging three hundred forty-two point one two four miles in seventy-two hours during the grueling competition. Her remarkable performance established her dominance in multi-day ultrarunning against international competitors like runner-up Simen Holvik. She reflected on the intense physical and mental journey immediately after crossing the finish line. It is the longest and the shortest thing, she said. There is so much that goes on, so many ups and downs. But we had a good time! It is going to take a long time to process.

stories.title: Treasury Department to buy back up to $6 billion in longer-term debt, triple the normal level
stories.summary:
The Treasury Department will buy back up to six billion dollars of government debt in an operation on Thursday. The twenty minute window concludes at two p.m. E. T. This triples the normal two billion dollar buyback operation for already issued securities. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated on August nineteenth that the department would at least double the normal amount. Future operations will be at least four billion dollars.

The measure targets ten and twenty year notes to keep government debt markets liquid. It attempts to put a lid on Treasury yields that hit highs not seen since before the two thousand eight global financial crisis. Market reaction was negative. Treasury yields rose further and remained volatile. Long dated securities rose as much as five basis points each before easing. The benchmark ten year issue hit four point eight four one percent around eleven thirty a.m. E. T. The twenty year climbed to five point three one four percent. The thirty year bond rose five basis points to five point three zero seven percent.

Higher yields have coincided with government debt passing forty trillion dollars. Other factors include inflation fears from tariffs and the Iran war. Crude oil has also topped one hundred dollars a barrel. Publicly held debt sits at thirty one point eight trillion dollars. That is up eight point two percent. Treasury issuance jumped eleven point eight percent from twenty twenty-five.

The move drew criticism for breaking predictable Treasury processes. It also failed to match speculation that buybacks could reach up to ten billion dollars. Bond fund manager, Mark Spindel, is the chief investment officer at Potomac River Capital. He said this is not Hank Paulson's bazooka. He also noted that crisis required an act of Congress. Stanley Druckenmiller, head of Duquesne Family Office, criticized the defense of prices in a Wall Street Journal op-ed. He wrote that once markets believe Treasury is defending a price, every rise in yields becomes a test of official resolve. He added that operations must grow to survive the tests.

stories.title: Ben Shelton wins a night of vomit, sweat and home hopes to triumph at US Open
stories.summary: Ben Shelton defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set quarter-final at the United States Open. The epic win started on Tuesday night and concluded on Wednesday morning. Ben Shelton fired seven aces during the grueling encounter to secure his historic tournament triumph. The match ended at three thirty-three a.m. at the Arthur Ashe Stadium. This marked the latest-ever finish at the tournament and the fifth-latest finish in grand slam history. Soccer star Trinity Rodman and Shelton's mother and sister watched the late-night match from the stands. The victory keeps alive a real chance of an American man winning the tournament for the first time since two thousand three.
stories.author: Andrew Lawrence at Flushing Meadows

stories.title: New satellite images show major construction surge at Iran’s Pickaxe nuke site
stories.summary:
Satellite imagery reviewed by C. N. N. reveals a sharp surge in construction activity in twenty twenty-six at Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain site. This suspected nuclear facility is buried beneath a granite mountain near the Natanz complex about one hundred forty miles south of Tehran.

The analysis was conducted by the Center for Strategic and International Studies and is based on six years of imagery. It shows the site has shifted from active excavation toward internal construction. There is also exterior reinforcement, road paving, and hardening of tunnel portal accesses.

Analysts indicated the facility is likely designed as a safe haven or housing for Iran's nuclear programme. It could serve as a potential centrifuge assembly plant, an enrichment facility, or a location for uranium metal conversion. However, it is not yet capable of enrichment work.

U. S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly threatened to strike the heavily fortified location. He stated last week that they may hit Pickaxe very soon. He also noted that they know everyone moving at the site.

The U. S. military maintains operational plans for strikes against Pickaxe Mountain using some of the largest bombs in its arsenal. The granite mountain presents a difficult target. A defence agency signed an emergency one point two million dollar contract justification for a subterranean test facility. Meanwhile, the U. S. military is currently developing a next generation penetrator bomb to reach deeply buried targets.
stories.author: YASHASVI VASISTHA

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange strikes as two killed at Moldova border
stories.summary: Two people were killed when Russian drones struck the Starokozache border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova. The strike forced the facility to close. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the aggression must be stopped here and now before it spreads any further. The overnight attack also injured three people, including a Moldovan driver. This was reported by Odesa regional head Oleh Kiper and the foreign ministry of Moldova. In the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv, a woman was killed and fourteen people were injured. That total includes two children after a Russian drone hit a nine storey residential building. In Russia, officials reported that four people were killed and twenty-nine others injured in a Ukrainian drone attack. The strike happened in the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk. Governor Veniamin Kondratiev described it as a massive overnight enemy drone attack. A child was among those killed in that port city. A drone also hit an industrial facility in the Arctic city of Novy Urengoy. That location is nearly three thousand kilometres from Ukraine. Falling wreckage triggered a fire there with no injuries reported, according to regional governor Dmitry Artyukhov. The defence ministry of Russia stated its forces shot down five hundred ninety-six Ukrainian drones overnight. The cross-border strikes occurred as Russia and Ukraine stepped up long-range attacks. This happened despite renewed diplomatic efforts following a phone call between Russian President Vladimir Putin and United States President Donald Trump about ending the war. Weekend meetings also took place in Moscow and Kyiv involving United States envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.

stories.title: BRICS leaders gather in India, but does the group have a clear purpose?
stories.summary:
India is hosting the eighteenth B. R. I. C. S. summit in Delhi this weekend. The slogan is Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. This reinterprets the original acronym for the five founding members of Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. It now includes new members Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates. The bloc now represents nearly half the world population and about forty percent of global G. D. P.

Mihaela Papa, director of the B. R. I. C. S. Lab at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, noted that India adds clout. It has significant geopolitical weight and relationships across competing camps. This makes it an important bridge builder.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian will attend. United Arab Emirates President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan is expected to send representatives. Saudi Arabia is also expected to attend even though its B. R. I. C. S. status remains somewhat ambiguous.

For host India, the summit serves as a platform for bilateral meetings. This includes a scheduled Friday meeting between Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It is also an opportunity for Modi and Xi to speak face to face amid continued strain in the China and India relationship.

Yale University lecturer Sushant Singh stated that concrete outcomes and what is achievable will likely be very limited. B. R. I. C. S. is simply not a priority for India. India is not comfortable with any kind of anti-western line. It focuses instead on defense ties with the U. S. and trade ties with the west as a whole.

Papa expects progress this weekend specifically in trade and agriculture. Progress will also involve monetary cooperation using an alternative financial architecture for currency exchange. She noted that India is keen for a coordinated approach from B. R. I. C. S. to trade and the World Trade Organization.

However, Singh maintains that internal contradictions will continue to make consensus difficult. These include a growing number of autocracies and tense bilateral relations among members.

stories.title: Iran says it hit American vessels, oil tankers in Hormuz in retaliation for U.S. strikes
stories.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps said they struck two American vessels and eight oil tankers in the Gulf. This was retaliation against the United States for destroying five Iranian tankers. The Guards stated the targeted vessels tried to cross a forbidden area of the Hormuz Strait.

United States Central Command reported that the American military destroyed five Iranian crude oil tankers on Tuesday. This happened after the Iranian Guard fired ballistic missiles at an American warship twice over the past two days. The targeted American warship successfully evaded the attack and no American personnel were harmed.

Central Command stated that United States forces struck four tankers in the Gulf of Oman. These were named the M T Kaviz, the M T Charminar, the M T Horizon one, and the M T Riesco. They also struck the M T Derya near Iran's Kharg Island. American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before rendering the vessels inoperable.

This exchange follows the United States military destroying three Iranian tankers on Saturday. That action was in response to the Guard firing ballistic missiles at an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer. The escalating conflict along a critical oil corridor has pushed Brent crude to near one hundred dollars a barrel.

Iranian Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, dismissed United States sanctions on the platform X as a rehash of a failed strategy.

In a separate incident on Tuesday, Central Command addressed an unmanned submersible that Iran reportedly seized in the Strait of Hormuz. United States Navy Captain, Tim Hawkins, stated that an underwater drone operated by United States forces malfunctioned more than a day ago while surveying regional waters. Hawkins dismissed the captured craft as an older and defective model. It carried no classified sonar or radar equipment and collected no sensitive data.

Iranian media outlets identified the sub as a Dive-L-D autonomous undersea vehicle developed by Anduril. The craft costs two point five million dollars each according to a twenty twenty-four DefenseScoop report. An Anduril spokesperson noted that the Dive-L-D is an attritable autonomous system designed to operate in dangerous environments where loss is expected.

stories.title: US strikes Iranian oil tankers as Tehran targets American base in Jordan
stories.summary:
United States forces struck five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday. They sank one tanker named, M/T Riesco. This followed two separate Iranian attempts to target an American warship.

United States Central Command stated that four of the targeted oil tankers were in the Gulf of Oman. They were linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards Corps. Another tanker was targeted near Kharg Island. Ninety percent of the country's crude oil passes through that part of the Gulf.

In retaliation, Iran launched twenty missiles at a United States base in Jordan. The Jordanian Armed Forces reported shooting down eighteen missiles. Two missiles fell in unpopulated areas.

The Revolutionary Guards also stated they attacked two United States vessels. They claimed to hit eight oil tankers and ten non-compliant vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. No American troops were harmed during the attacks.

The strikes followed an earlier incident where Iran claimed to have seized a malfunctioning uncrewed United States submarine. United States Navy Captain, Tim Hawkins noted the recovered underwater drone was an older model. It carried no classified equipment.

The latest exchanges follow more than six months of escalation. This started after initial United States and Israeli attacks on Iran on February twenty-eighth.

The United States military justified Tuesday's maritime strikes. They identified the targeted tankers as part of a multi-billion-dollar shadow network. This network funds the I. R. G. C. and regional proxies.

United States Secretary of State, Marco Rubio stated that Iran will lose a tanker every time they try to hit United States naval ships.

Regional instability widened on Tuesday. Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement launched drone and missile attacks. They targeted energy and civilian infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. The attacks injured seventy-three people. They caused temporary halts at oil facilities.

The growing conflict pushed oil markets higher in Asia trading. Benchmark Brent crude rose one point five percent to ninety-nine dollars and thirty-five cents a barrel. United States traded oil increased one point three percent to ninety-four dollars and twenty-three cents.

stories.title: Hackers Breach F5 BIG-IP APM Devices to Deploy Linux Rootkit
stories.summary: Attackers are targeting F5 B. I. G. dash I. P. A. P. M. environments with a new Linux rootkit. Security researchers from Sophos and E. S. E. T. track this malware as PoisonedRefresh. The attackers likely deployed the payload after exploiting C. V. E. dash twenty twenty-five dash fifty-three five hundred twenty-one. This is a critical remote code execution flaw. F. S. Networks reclassified it from a denial-of-service problem in March. The malicious installer infected the Apache executable on B. I. G. dash I. P. A. P. M. systems. It also modified S. E. Linux configurations and maintained persistence across B. I. G. dash I. P. A. P. M. upgrade images. Sophos researchers stated that the second-stage sample hides key operational strings with R. C. four. It gains execution before the host application main function is invoked by intercepting libc start main. The malware targets the Apache P. H. P. module by hooking the Apache Portable Runtime module loader. Then it injects a P. H. P. web shell into memory. The implant intercepts P. H. P. file operations. It hides the web shell inside legitimate scripts like apm css dot php three and full wt dot php three and webtop popup css dot php three. This leaves files on disk unchanged to reduce detection. The injected web shell processes magic requests. It executes them via P. H. P. eval and returns an H. T. T. P. two hundred one response disguised as C. S. S. content. The rootkit also includes a protection mechanism. It delays local backdoor creation to prevent service disruption. Furthermore it creates a password-protected local communication socket. This socket launches an interactive Bash shell without using a T. C. P. listening port. The ShadowServer Foundation reported that seven hundred ninety-five vulnerable F. S. B. I. G. dash I. P. A. P. M. endpoints were exposed online yesterday. Defenders are advised to investigate unusual P. O. S. T. requests to targeted dot php three endpoints. They should also look for responses combining H. T. T. P. two hundred one with a text slash c. s. s. content type.

stories.title: 220M Traveler Records Exposed in Vietnam-Linked APIS Leak
stories.summary:
A massive database containing traveler and crew records was exposed online. Researchers at, Kinryū Labs discovered the leak.

The exposed database held over two hundred twenty million records. It leaked due to a chain of security misconfigurations.

The researchers found the exposed cluster on June third. They were surveying databases as part of research into ransomware activity.

The cluster was hosted in Hanoi. It held approximately one hundred seven gigabytes of data across twenty-nine indices.

The records included over two hundred ten million passenger entries. They also included over ten million crew entries.

The data spanned from January twenty-fourseen to April twenty twenty-six.

The exposed information featured names and dates of birth. It also included sex and nationalities and passport numbers.

Other exposed fields included document expiration dates and issuing countries. Flight numbers and airlines were also exposed.

Departure and destination airports were in the data. Seat assignments and baggage references and flight times were exposed too.

Sample records reviewed by BleepingComputer included travelers of various nationalities. These included Korean and Chinese and Canadian and New Zealand nationalities.

The researchers accessed the database by chaining two misconfigurations. They overcame an initial H. T. T. P. four hundred one unauthorized response.

They used a cloud-based path that accepted default credentials.

An internet intelligence platform named, FOFA first recorded the host and port in October twenty twenty-two. The exact duration of the exposure remains unknown.

Kinryū Labs reported the vulnerability to Vietnamese authorities on June third. They also reported it to airlines and national computer emergency response teams.

Access to the database was remediated on June eighth. Singapore Airlines security team helped secure it.

Vietnamese authorities did not respond to requests for comment. It remains unclear whether malicious actors accessed or copied the data before it was secured.

Researchers found no server logs or ransom notes. They also found no unfamiliar indices.

stories.title: WeWorm
stories.summary:
Security firm Calif has released a demo of a new threat called WeWorm. It is the first zero click worm to spread through WeChat calls across I. O. S. and Android devices. Working with A. I., the team found a memory corruption bug in the app. They built a remote code execution exploit in about two days. Then they built the worm in one more week.

The exploit lets an attacker on a victim friend list hijack a WeChat account while the phone is ringing. The user does not need to answer or touch the device at all. By compromising one account, the worm can automatically call and infect other contacts on both Android and I. O. S. platforms.

Calif reported the vulnerability to Tencent in July of twenty twenty-six. Tencent confirmed on August twenty-eighth that the exploit had been fixed on the server side for all users. Calif is keeping full technical details secret until an upcoming conference. The research highlights how A. I. is lowering the barrier for creating sophisticated cyber threats.

stories.title: LIV files for bankruptcy protection with over $45m owed to players
stories.summary:
L. I. V. Golf filed for Chapter eleven bankruptcy protection in the federal district court of New Jersey on Tuesday. At least forty-five million dollars is owed to fourteen current and former players for the third quarter of twenty twenty-six.

The filing follows a decision in April by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund to pull its multibillion-dollar funding. The fund spent more than five billion dollars since the league launched in twenty twenty-one. Court documents estimate L. I. V. assets between one hundred million and five hundred million dollars. Liabilities are estimated between five hundred million and one billion dollars.

Two-time major winner, Jon Rahm tops the list of the thirty largest unsecured creditors. His claim is seven point five million dollars. Bryson DeChambeau follows at five point seven million dollars. Dustin Johnson is owed five point five million dollars. Cameron Smith is owed four point eight million dollars. Tyrrell Hatton is owed three point four million dollars. Brooks Koepka is owed one point seven million dollars.

The Public Investment Fund is providing a forty-nine point six million dollar bankruptcy loan to help fund the restructuring process. L. I. V. found a new proposed investor in B. C. Partners. The league intends to launch a new majority player-owned league early next year under a more sustainable business model. Field sizes will expand to seventy-five players. The league will introduce a cut and lower prize purses than the P. G. A. Tour.

Previous player contracts will finish due to the court filing. Players now have the option to leave without any obligation to sign on to the new league. Speaking before the Irish Open on Tuesday, Jon Rahm told the B. B. C. that he still has a contract with L. I. V. one point zero that he is more than willing to fulfil. He added that time will tell.

stories.title: Probe ordered into police action against protesting Bhopal intern doctors
stories.summary:
Bhopal Police Commissioner Sanjay Kumar ordered an inquiry into police action against protesting M. B. B. S. intern doctors. The directive came from Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister Rajendra Shukla.

On September seventh, twenty twenty-six, hundreds of interns from Gandhi Medical College protested on their campus. They demanded a stipend hike from fourteen thousand four hundred thirty-seven rupees to thirty thousand rupees.

Protestors planned a march toward the Chief Minister residence. Police deployed water cannons and resorted to a baton charge near the campus. This stopped the march less than two kilometers from the destination.

At least four interns suffered serious injuries. These included a broken arm and an eye injury.

Interns launched an overnight sit-in at Kamla Park on September seventh and eighth. They boycotted outpatient department and routine operation theatre services while maintaining emergency care. Services were also disrupted at Gajra Raja Medical College in solidarity.

Siddhartha Kumar Rai, president of the Junior Doctors Association undergraduate student wing, spoke about the event. He stated that the peaceful protestors work thirty-six hour duties and handle heavy patient loads, yet they were treated like goons.

Kavita N. Singh criticized the police action in a letter to Commissioner Kumar. She called the use of force without prior notice completely inappropriate. She demanded action against responsible officers.

Vikas Sahwal, Deputy Commissioner of Police for Zone two, has been appointed to conduct an impartial investigation.

stories.title: US strikes Iranian tankers after attempted missile attacks on its Navy warship: Report
stories.summary: On Tuesday, September eighth, the United States struck multiple Iranian oil tankers.  This followed attempted missile attacks that targeted a U. S. Navy warship.  The Associated Press reported the strikes, citing an anonymous U. S. official.  Iranian media separately reported that a U. S. projectile struck a small tanker about four miles from Kharg Island.  Kharg Island is a key oil export hub, and no casualties were reported from that strike.  Blasts were also heard on Kharg Island and in the southern port of Jask.  Ahead of the strikes, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy warned tanker crews near Kuwait and Bahrain to immediately leave their vessels.  They stated the ships would be targeted.  Iranian Armed Forces chief of staff, Ali Abdollahi warned that Tehran would target U. S. military bases across the region in retaliation.  Meanwhile, the Revolutionary Guard stated it intercepted and destroyed an M. Q.-one drone over the Strait of Hormuz using a new advanced defence system.  The military escalation drove international benchmark Brent crude to briefly reach ninety-nine dollars and forty-six cents a barrel on Tuesday.  In tandem with the strikes, the U. S. Treasury announced sanctions against thirty-six entities.  The sanctions target all remaining Iranian airlines not previously penalized.  Officials accused the aviation sector of transporting weapons and illicit cargo.  Despite the military escalation, Iran stated that diplomatic efforts were making progress.  Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi noted that talks with Oman on managing the strategic waterway had achieved significant progress.  Meanwhile, U. S. Secretary of State, Marco Rubio accused Iran of orchestrating recent attacks by Houthi rebels against Saudi Arabia.  In Lebanon, Israeli airstrikes in the south on Monday killed thirteen people.  The Lebanese Health Ministry provided this casualty count, marking an escalation after weeks of calm.

stories.title: Iran launched fresh attack on US navy ships Monday amid China, Russia aid fears
stories.summary: Iran launched a fresh attack targeting United States navy ships on Monday. This followed similar ballistic missile strikes over the weekend. Those weekend strikes were aimed at a United States aircraft carrier and a guided missile destroyer. No United States warships were hit in the incidents. The incidents have not yet been acknowledged by the United States military. In response to the weekend carrier targeting, the United States struck three Iranian oil tankers. Washington stated those tankers were funding the military of Iran and proxy groups. The repeated attacks have raised concerns among United States officials. Officials are concerned that Iran is employing more advanced weapons. Iran is also potentially receiving tracking assistance from China or Russia. Iranian state media claimed the country is using new missiles with advanced technology. Weapons analysts note these could include electro optical seekers. Those seekers use images to adjust trajectories toward moving targets., John Caves, a senior research associate at the Wisconsin Project on Nuclear Arms Control, stated something important. He stated that Iran unveiled the Qassem Bassir medium range ballistic missile with such seeker technology last year. He also stated that other Iranian missiles, including the Khalij Fars, use it too. The escalation comes as a United States blockade of Iranian ports increases economic pressure on the country. A United States navy official noted that nineteen warships are currently supporting operations in the Middle East. Washington has warned it will respond to attacks on its naval vessels. The United States hopes sanctions will ultimately force Iranian leadership to back down.
stories.author: ABHISHEK MISHRA

stories.title: New report shows the economic toll of ICE raids
stories.summary:
Immigration crackdowns that began in early twenty twenty-five drained over one point two six billion dollars from local businesses in Cook County, Illinois. A new study from the University of Illinois Chicago revealed these findings using anonymous cellphone G. P. S. data. Regular travel between immigrant and non-immigrant neighborhoods collapsed almost immediately after President Donald Trump took office on January twentieth, twenty twenty-five, amid rumors and sweeps of I. C. E. raids.

This decreased consumer mobility cost retail shops and restaurants in non-immigrant areas approximately one point two six billion dollars. It also cost Illinois one hundred seven million dollars in lost tax revenue. Co-author Professor Matt Wilson told N. P. R. that the city has yet to recover. He stated they saw a nine percent drop in retail and a ten percent drop in restaurant visits. These drops persisted for about a year with systematically changed consumer behavior.

Nationwide, the administration policies resulted in hundreds of thousands of arrests. The immigration detention population sits at a record high of approximately sixty-five thousand people. White House spokesperson Lauren Bis defended the enforcement strategy in a statement to N. P. R. She said that removing criminals makes communities safer. She added that nearly seventy percent of I. C. E. arrests are of illegal aliens charged or convicted of a crime.

Meanwhile, I. C. E. statistics show that roughly seventy percent of those currently detained have no criminal convictions. The report also highlights broader economic impacts across the country. Minneapolis saw an estimated seven hundred million dollars in total economic damage. Small businesses there lost over eighty-one million dollars in January alone. The Brookings Institution also estimated a one point seven percentage point decline in aggregate consumer spending in high enforcement states.
stories.author: Jasmine Garsd

stories.title: NIH to use part of its budget to pay for Department of Defense research
stories.summary:
The National Institutes of Health has reached an agreement to fund research at the Department of Defense. The deal will run for ten years. It creates a system to transfer money for staff and projects. These projects support the advanced development of medical countermeasures against pandemic influenza. They also target chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats, along with emerging infectious diseases.

The funds will come from the budget of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases. That institute received an allocation of six point six billion dollars from Congress in twenty twenty-six. The exact transfer amount remains unspecified. However, reporting by Nature indicates the Department of Defense initially sought up to a third of its total budget. It was later told to settle for roughly ten percent.

The agreement comes as the twenty twenty-six defense budget sits at approximately one trillion dollars. That budget faces strain from the conflict with Iran. At the same time, the National Institutes of Health struggles to issue sufficient grants to use the money allocated to it by Congress.
stories.author: John Timmer

stories.title: UK announces sanctions on West Bank settlements prompting furious Israeli response
stories.summary: The United Kingdom has announced a comprehensive sanctions regime targeting illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. This bans settlement goods and advertising and services linked to settlement expansion. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told members of parliament that the action marks the beginning of a new approach to the conflict. He launched the action alongside France and Canada. He accused the Israeli government of turning a blind eye to the ethnic cleansing of Palestinians by settlers. Miliband stated that the United Kingdom views the occupation as unlawful. He cited a twenty twenty-four advisory opinion from the International Court of Justice. He announced that the new sanctions will be introduced over the next six to nine months. The decision follows Israel opening tenders to build approximately one thousand two hundred settlement homes in the E1 area east of Jerusalem. Israel Foreign Minister Gideon Saar denounced the move as an outrageous lie. He shut the United Kingdom consulate in East Jerusalem. Israel banned eleven United Kingdom members of parliament from entering the country. Israel retaliated by terminating British military training programs. Saar stated that the hostile Labour government left Israel no choice but to respond. President Isaac Herzog warned the decision would fall on the wrong side of history. The United Kingdom also issued a joint statement with eleven other nations pledging support for the two-state solution and restricting trade with settlements.

stories.title: German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
stories.summary:
The far-right extremist A. F. D. has won the state election in Saxony-Anhalt. It is a landslide victory that leaves the governing C. D. U. barely half as strong as before. The party is now positioned to potentially put forward the state minister-president.

Commerzbank economist, Ralph Solveen, told Reuters that an A. F. D. led government would be a turning point. He advised waiting because major economic decisions on taxes, labor structures, and social security are made at the federal level.

Michael Berlemann, director of the Hamburg Institute of International Economics, stated much of the A. F. D. migration policy cannot be implemented at the state level. Courts would likely overturn it. However, he warned that the indirect impacts remain problematic.

Berlemann warned that announced measures mean skilled workers in health care, hospitality, agriculture, and construction will avoid the state. This will exacerbate labor shortages and widen the economic gap.

I. N. G. chief economist, Carsten Brzeski, added that symbolic headlines about forced deportations will deter foreign skilled workers. He noted that Saxony-Anhalt is not the entire German economy.

Business associations and economic institutes called for federal action in response to the outcome. D. I. W. President, Marcel Fratzscher, described the result as a vote of no confidence in the federal government. He urged Berlin to implement far-reaching structural reforms.

Tanja Gönner, managing director of the Federation of German Industries, said the response must not be political paralysis. She stated the federal government must consistently implement reforms to boost investment, innovation, and growth.

stories.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: A predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome
stories.summary: Google DeepMind introduces the AlphaGenome Atlas, a one petabyte database created by the AlphaGenome artificial intelligence model. The human genome contains about three billion base pairs of DNA, where two percent code for proteins and ninety-eight percent remain less understood. The database pre calculates the regulatory impact of all nine billion single letter genetic changes. The Atlas introduces the AlphaGenome Variant Impact score to combine predictions for coding and non coding regions. At the Broad Institute, Laura Covill and her team used the score to identify a critical variant in the D N M one gene that created an incorrect splice site for unsolved rare disease research. Dr. Gareth Hawkes applied the tool to data from fifty-four thousand plus U K Biobank participants, uncovering twenty-two percent more non coding genetic associations and identifying nineteen genetic regions linked to body mass index. The AlphaGenome Atlas is available through a website portal requiring zero coding skills. A massive collaborative research project credits dozens of individuals and major institutions for their work. The institutions include the University of Exeter and Harvard University. Researchers from Boston Children's Hospital and the Broad Institute also contributed. The Stowers Institute for Medical Research joined as a collaborator. The Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center contributed to developing the work. stories.title: Mistral raises €3B
stories.summary:
Mistral has raised three billion euros in a Series D funding round. The post-money valuation is more than twenty-one billion euros. This is the largest equity fundraising round ever completed by a European technology company. It happened three years after the launch of Mistral. Samsung Electronics led the round. Co-leads include Scaleup Europe Fund managed by E. Q. T. Existing investor P. S. G. Equity also co-led. New investors joining the round include Advent and funds and accounts managed by BlackRock. The Grand Duchy of Luxembourg joined as well. Numerous existing investors participated. They include a one-six-z, A. S. M. L., and N. V. I. D. I. A.

The funding will expand frontier research at Mistral. It will scale compute capacity for training powerful models. It will accelerate commercial growth and widen the international footprint. Mistral currently operates across twenty countries. It supports more than one hundred twenty-five global enterprises. These include Airbus, A. S. M. L., and H. S. B. C. The company states it is the only A. I. company building a full stack of open-weight models. It builds infrastructure and compute capacity. It builds production products to meet growing international demand. This demand is for A. I. performance combined with data governance and independence. It also offers control over infrastructure and the intelligence loop.
stories.author: kuberwastaken

stories.title: N-able patches max-severity N-central flaw amid ongoing attacks
stories.summary:
N-able has released an emergency hotfix for a maximum-severity remote code execution vulnerability. The flaw affects the N-central remote monitoring and management platform. It is tracked as C. V. E. dash twenty twenty-six dash eighty-six thousand two hundred eighteen. The flaw allows unprivileged threat actors to execute malicious code on unpatched systems. These online-exposed instances are vulnerable to low-complexity attacks.

N-able addressed the issue on Saturday. They issued N-central twenty twenty-six point three Hotfix four. The company is urging customers to upgrade immediately. The Shadowserver Foundation tracks nearly fifteen hundred N-central servers exposed online. These servers are primarily located in the United States and Europe.

N-able stated it has no confirmations that the vulnerability is being targeted. However, cybersecurity company Huntress flagged it as a potential zero-day. They also flagged two high-severity vulnerabilities tracked as C. V. E. dash twenty twenty-six dash eighty-six thousand two hundred six and C. V. E. dash twenty twenty-six dash eighty-six thousand two hundred seven. These two flaws were also patched over the weekend.

Huntress noted it could not definitively determine if these flaws were responsible for an exploitation. This exploitation was seen in a customer patched production environment. Logs on the compromised server had already rotated. In an advisory, Huntress warned that on-premises users must apply Hotfix four immediately. Systems running Hotfix three remain vulnerable. Customers running on-premises deployments were instructed by N-able to upgrade to N-central twenty twenty-six point three H. F. four immediately to protect their environments.

stories.title: XPeng starts IRON humanoid robot production as Tesla Optimus stalls
stories.summary: Chinese automaker XPeng has activated the world first automated production line for advanced humanoid robots. The facility is located in Guangzhou. The first IRON robot walked off the line under its own power. Chief Executive Officer, He Xiaopeng stated that the production lines were created from scratch with no precedent. The production setup features more than eighty percent core process automation. It borrows quality systems used for electric cars. The company robotics arm recently raised over nine hundred million dollars. That was at a six point three billion dollar valuation. The funding round was led by, I. D. G. Capital. Tencent and Alibaba also participated. The IRON robot features seventy-six degrees of freedom across its body. It has twenty-one degrees of freedom in each hand. Three in-house Turing A. I. chips power the machine. They deliver up to two thousand two hundred fifty T. O. P. S. These chips run its Physical A. I. foundation model without remote teleoperation. This news matters because XPeng is attempting to solve a difficult challenge. That challenge is consistently manufacturing generalized humanoid robots at scale. XPeng is targeting mass production by the end of twenty twenty-six. Initial deployments are planned for its own stores and campuses. Commercial sales and deliveries will begin in China and abroad in twenty twenty-seven. The company aims to build over one thousand robots a month. This is on the way to one million robots a year by twenty thirty.
